paragraphs.text: The Medes: the inhabitants of the kingdom of Media, which is bounded on the north and east by the Caspian Sea, on the south by Persia, and on the west by the kingdom of Assyria (present-day Iraq). Arphaxad is the one called "Phraortes," that is, "the great king," or "Phra," that is, king, to which "Kshad," that is, "the gentle," was then added. All of these are names of one king, who was titled the great and gentle king. He was great because he built the great city "Achmetha," and gentle because he loved the Jews and was kind to them. He was the son of King "Deioces," who began the building of Achmetha, and then Arphaxad completed its building.
It is evident that this Arphaxad was strong and great, and was able to triumph over many peoples around him and to enlarge the kingdom of "Media."
To confirm his greatness he built a great city which he called "Achmetha," or "Ecbatana," and made it the capital of the land of Media. It is near the present city of Tehran in Iran.

The great King Arphaxad took care to build his capital Achmetha with the highest degree of strength and grandeur. He built its houses of squared blocks of stone and made its walls very high and massive, proclaiming the impregnability of his city and his power. The height of the wall was seventy cubits (the cubit ranges between

45-50 cm) – that is, the cubit of a man – or about thirty-five meters, while the breadth of the wall was thirty cubits, or about fifteen meters approximately, so that the wall became like a broad road on which chariots and soldiers could be assembled.

To magnify his city he built towers on the wall, reaching a height of one hundred cubits, or about fifty meters. They were square towers, each side about twenty feet long (the foot being 30 cm), that is, about six meters.

As for the gates of the city, he made them very high and massive like towers, reaching a height of fifty meters, so that the greatness of his armies would be seen when they marched out of them. And Arphaxad became haughty and boasted of his power and the greatness of his armies.

This is man in every generation: he relies on material things and thinks by this that he has fortified himself, but "Except the Lord keep the house, the watchman waketh but in vain" (Ps 126:1-2). This great city was destroyed shortly afterward, just as all the material things on which man relies vanish, and nothing remains except "the name of the Lord, which is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10). So I wish, my brother, that you would be humble and thank God for His gifts, and not exalt yourself over those around you, but be like your Master, who sat at the feet of His disciples.

entries.section: (2) The victory of Nabuchodonosor over Arphaxad

paragraphs.text: Tigris and Euphrates: the two main rivers of Iraq.
Jadason: a river located in the east of Iraq.
Elymeans: that is, Elam, a country located east of Iraq.
Ragau: that is, Rhages. This region is located east of Iraq, at the border of the king of the Elymeans.

Nabuchodonosor, king of Assyria (which neighbors Media on the west), whose capital was Nineveh (located on the river Tigris), feared the growing power of Arphaxad and his control over the neighboring kingdoms. So in the twelfth year of his reign Nabuchodonosor decided to make war against Arphaxad, king of Media. He is not the same as Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, who came at a later time and defeated the kingdom of Assyria, since Nebuchadnezzar is a title given to some of the kings of Assyria and Babylon and means "protector of the land," and his real name was "Esarhaddon." So he marched toward Arphaxad with great armies and met him in the plain of "Ragau."

The wars between Nabuchodonosor and Arphaxad continued for five years, until the seventeenth year of Nabuchodonosor's reign (according to the modern edition of the Jesuit Fathers). In the end he triumphed over him and took possession of his land.

entries.section: (3) The messages of Nabuchodonosor to the lands of the West

paragraphs.text: Cilicia: a province located in the southeast of Asia Minor, that is, Turkey.
Damascus: the capital of present-day Syria, an ancient city from the days of our father Abraham.
Lebanon: the present country of Lebanon, which lies on the Mediterranean Sea, north of Jordan and Palestine.

Nabuchodonosor repeated the error of Arphaxad: he became proud and sought to dominate the lands of the world around him. So he sent messengers to the lands of Cilicia, Damascus and Lebanon, that is, what corresponds today to the region of Turkey, Syria and Lebanon.

entries.section: (3) The messages of Nabuchodonosor to the lands of the West

paragraphs.text: Carmel: a mountain range located east of Lebanon.
Cedar: one of the most important Arab tribes that dwelt in the north of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Saudi Arabia.
Galilee: the northern region of the land of the Jews, that is, Canaan, and most of its inhabitants were Gentiles. Esdraelon: a region located in the north of Galilee.
He also sent to the regions of Carmel, Cedar, Galilee and Esdraelon, that is, what corresponds today to Lebanon, northern Saudi Arabia and northern Palestine.

entries.section: (3) The messages of Nabuchodonosor to the lands of the West

paragraphs.text: Samaria: a fortified city to which many lands were subject, located in the middle part of the land of the Jews, that is, ancient Canaan, between Galilee in the north and Judea in the south. It was the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel when it was divided in the days of Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
Beyond Jordan to Jerusalem: this includes all the lands surrounding the river Jordan and extends to the north of Egypt. Its most important city is Jerusalem, which lies southwest of the Jordan.
The land of Jesse: the whole land of the Jews, which expanded in the days of King David the son of Jesse and extends from the river Jordan to the borders of Egypt.

He also sent to the land of Samaria and the regions surrounding the river Jordan as far as the borders of Egypt and Ethiopia, that is, he sent to all the lands of the Jews and also to Ethiopia. So the king's messengers reached all the lands mentioned above.

So it is that pride is the mother of many sins: it leads to greed, the exploitation of others, and contempt for them. Therefore humility is also the father of many virtues, and it – that is, humility – is greatly hated by Satan, because it gives man the joy of fellowship with God through various virtues.

entries.section: (3) The messages of Nabuchodonosor to the lands of the West

paragraphs.text: When the messages of Nabuchodonosor reached all the lands, they too fell into pride and made light of him. They agreed not to submit to him, and drove out his messengers with contempt, relying on their own strength and despising him. This was the way known at that time to express objection to messages: insulting those who carried them.

entries.section: (3) The messages of Nabuchodonosor to the lands of the West

paragraphs.text: When the messengers returned to Nabuchodonosor, he was very angry and swore by his throne that he would take vengeance on all these lands. This shows his pride, which inclines toward deifying himself: he does not swear by the pagan gods, but swears by his throne and his authority.

So they met his pride with their own pride, and of course pride does not cure pride, but rather inflames it more. The only solution is humility, so that God's mercies overflow upon the humble man and he overcomes all his enemies, just as Christ – by His humility on the cross – conquered all the pride of the devil and his authority.
The army advanced on the surrounding countries

entries.section: (1) The king's decision to take possession of all the earth

paragraphs.text: The first month: that is, the month of Nisan, which corresponds to the present month of April. This month is the first in the Babylonian year.

After the reign of Nabuchodonosor king of Assyria was established and he had triumphed over Arphaxad king of the Medes, he resolved in himself to take vengeance on all the lands that had refused to submit to him. In his pride he wanted to occupy the whole world around him and set himself up as a god over the peoples. He chose a suitable time to prepare the army and attack, which was the season of spring, so this agreement took place in the month of April.

entries.section: (1) The king's decision to take possession of all the earth

paragraphs.text: He communicated his secret counsel to them: he agreed with them on a plan of war.

The king gathered his counselors, the elders, and likewise the commanders of his armies, and agreed with them on a plan of war to take vengeance on all his enemies who had refused to submit to him and to receive his messengers.

entries.section: (1) The king's decision to take possession of all the earth

paragraphs.text: The king agreed with his counselors and his commanders on his decision, which he had taken in himself in pride, to subject the whole world to himself.

This is the insatiable greed of man: whenever God gives him a grace, he asks for more. He does not thank God but grows more boastful of himself, and in the end he loses everything, because he did not know the source of his grace, that is, God, and did not delight in fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the army and its needs

paragraphs.text: Holofernes: a Persian name meaning God appeared, or revealed.

The king's counselors and the commander of his armies were pleased with the king's idea of founding an empire that would subject the whole world to itself. It seems that the king's pride and conceit passed to his helpers, so they praised his idea and supported it with all their hearts, which led him to go further and take practical steps. He summoned the greatest of his military commanders – perhaps he had not been present at this session because of special circumstances, or he was present and the king took him aside to give him specific orders regarding his desire to subject the whole world to himself – so that he would attack all the cities around him throughout the inhabited world, fortified and unfortified, and destroy them violently, especially those who had made light of his messengers and refused to submit to him. Most of these kingdoms lie to the west of Assyria.

So it is with man: when he is enraged he rushes into actions that may seem logical although they are wrong and spring from the pride of his heart, because "the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God" (Jas 1:20). Beware, then, of taking any decision when you are angry; rather wait until you calm down, then pray and make your decisions.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the army and its needs

paragraphs.text: Holofernes the commander began to prepare the army. He gathered one hundred and twenty thousand fighting men on foot, and of the horsemen able to use arrows and bows he gathered twelve thousand, so that he had a great and mighty army. In his pride he felt able to subdue the whole earth, forgetting that there is a power greater than he, which is God.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the army and its needs

paragraphs.text: Herds: flocks.

Holofernes began to gather provisions for his long journey. He gathered camels, cattle and sheep that were hard to count, to supply his soldiers with rich food, bearing in mind that the huge number of the army needed no fewer than four thousand sheep daily to feed it, or the equivalent in cattle and other kinds of livestock. Thus we can imagine the enormity of the herds that accompanied this mighty army. This shows how fearful the sight of this army was to the lands toward which it was moving, and also God's overwhelming power over this great army, in addition to the abundance of the spoil from which the children of God benefit when they triumph over this army. It is to be noted that the camels and other beasts, such as donkeys and mules, were for carrying personal baggage such as tents, clothing and the tools of daily living, in addition to spare weapons.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the army and its needs

paragraphs.text: Corn: wheat.

Because Syria was distinguished by its cultivation of wheat, he commanded that the grain be gathered from its farms when he attacked it and took possession of its cities, so that it would meet the needs of the army, which needs at least forty tons of wheat daily for its food.

From this we understand how confident Holofernes was that he would triumph over all the lands he would meet and take possession of their spoil and their crops. He was very conceited and relied on the strength of his army.

entries.section: (2) Preparing the army and its needs

paragraphs.text: King Nabuchodonosor gave Holofernes countless quantities of gold and silver to pay the salaries of the officers and soldiers, so that their morale would be high and they would fight bravely in their wars.

If man knows how to gather the needs of his journeys on earth from various material things, do you prepare what your journey to heaven requires, of spiritual worship, prayers, fasts and all works of mercy? And do you prepare the spiritual weapon, to overcome the wars of the devil and subdue him under your feet, so that you reach your goal, which is the Kingdom? I wish that you would not be sparing toward yourself in any spiritual striving, to ensure your victory, and God will help you according to your concern and your love for Him.

entries.section: (3) The devastation of the surrounding lands

paragraphs.text: His chariots: the war chariots.

After preparing the great army, Holofernes began to move out of Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, where King Nebuchadnezzar dwelt. The army included foot soldiers and horsemen, with bows and arrows, and the riders of the war chariots. Their number was very great, covering several kilometers, so they resembled swarms of locusts that cover vast areas when they attack any country.

entries.section: (3) The devastation of the surrounding lands

paragraphs.text: Assyria: a kingdom located in the north of Iraq, which expanded and extended to include almost the whole world of that time. Here the kingdom of Assyria before its expansion is meant.
The great mountains of Ange: a mountain range located in the west of Asia Minor, that is, western Turkey.

He describes here in general what this great army reached. It moved out of Nineveh and swept through many lands until it reached Turkey and the great mountains of Ange, on which many fortresses had been built, and it was able to take possession of all these lands; even these fortresses fell into its hand.
Put: a large city located in western Turkey.
The children of Tharsis: tribes that dwelt mostly in the wilderness of western Turkey, then migrated and settled in southern Spain.
The children of Ishmael: tribes that dwelt in the Arabian Peninsula, then migrated to dwell in the wilderness of western Turkey, and they had many herds.
Chelon: a city located in southern Turkey.

He lists here the lands that Holofernes took possession of. He destroyed and occupied many cities and places in western Turkey, such as Put, the children of Tharsis, the children of Ishmael and the land of Chelon.

entries.section: (3) The devastation of the surrounding lands

paragraphs.text: Euphrates: a great river in Iraq.
The sea: the Mediterranean Sea.
The valley of Mambre: in southern Palestine, east of the Mediterranean Sea; it was also called the city of Hebron, in which Abraham dwelt.

He mentions here other lands that Holofernes took possession of, which lie between the rivers Tigris and Euphrates in Iraq. He also took possession of lands in southern Palestine, such as the valley of Mambre. We note that the writer here is not bound to the route of the army, but mentions the various lands the army took possession of, until the whole world was subject to Nabuchodonosor. He mentions here some of the lands and not all of them, and he singles out the strong fortified lands, or the peoples and regions from which he took his needs, such as the cattle from the children of Tharsis and the children of Ishmael, and the wheat and barley from Syria. This explains the difference between the list of lands mentioned in this chapter and the one mentioned in the previous chapter, for he does not mention here all the lands he took possession of, but only some of them.

entries.section: (3) The devastation of the surrounding lands

paragraphs.text: The borders of Japheth which are toward the south: they lie south of the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea as far as western Turkey.
He took possession of many lands lying on the southern borders of Japheth, which are northeast of Nineveh as far as the north of the Mediterranean Sea in the west.

entries.section: (3) The devastation of the surrounding lands

paragraphs.text: The children of Madian: the inhabitants of Midian, which lies east of the Gulf of Aqaba.
He also took possession of the tribes of Midian and took their spoil of many herds, and killed everyone of them who opposed him.

entries.section: (3) The devastation of the surrounding lands

paragraphs.text: He went to the lands of Syria and took from them the wheat, the crops and the fruits, and that was in the days of harvest, that is, about the month of May. This means that he continued this campaign for more than a year, for he began his campaign when he went out from Nineveh in the month of April (ch. 1), and it is unreasonable that he took possession of all these lands within two months, so this expedition took more than a year. And after he had taken his needs of grain, he burned the rest of the fields and the trees, to weaken these lands so that they would become subject to him.

entries.section: (3) The devastation of the surrounding lands

paragraphs.text: So we see that this army was very fearful in all the lands of the world, so they submitted to it, and the resistance was very weak, not worth mentioning.

So the devil displays his material power to terrify the hearts of the children of God, but he is powerless before those who believe in the power of God, so he fears them and trembles if they are confident in their God. And the devil, if he could, would destroy our whole life cruelly, for our enemy, as the Holy Bible says, is "as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour" (1 Pet 5:8), but he cannot, because "If God be for us, who can be against us?" (Rom 8:31). The complete submission to Holofernes

entries.section: (1) The surrender of all the lands

paragraphs.text: Sent: dispatched.

When the lands were seized with fear and terror of the great army of Holofernes, which destroyed every land it met, they sent messengers to Holofernes from the rest of the lands, among them the lands of Syria, that is, the Levant, which extends from Iraq to the Mediterranean and as far as distant lands such as Libya. All of them begged for his kindness and asked to submit to him.

entries.section: (1) The surrender of all the lands

paragraphs.text: Subjection: humiliation.

The messengers said to Holofernes, "Our lands are ready to be enslaved to you and to King Nabuchodonosor, for this is better than that you should kill us and destroy our lands." This shows the extent of the weakness, despair and humiliation to which they had come, so they surrendered completely.

entries.section: (1) The surrender of all the lands

paragraphs.text: Lord of peace: a peaceful ruler who neither kills nor destroys.

In their surrender the messengers offered Holofernes their lands with all their cities, mountains and fields, and also their various possessions of cattle, goats, camels and horses. They delivered themselves to him as slaves, old and young, and declared their readiness to obey him in all his commands. Their only request was that he should not harm them and their lands, but leave them to live in peace, since they saw that his power could not be resisted.

Do not fear the terror and power of the devil, and do not surrender and become enslaved to him and to your lusts, and to the pressures of his wicked helpers around you in the world, for fear that you may die. Rather, be confident that death is a passing over to life, which is better than being humbled under the hand of the hard-hearted devil.

entries.section: (2) Conscripting the men from the captured cities

paragraphs.text: So Holofernes advanced with his great army and came down upon all the lands that had sent to appease him, and took possession of them. He chose the young men and the strong men able to fight and added them to his army, so that he had supporters from the lands he had taken possession of, and the strength of his army increased.

Holofernes, who is a type of Satan, if you surrender to him, is not satisfied with this, but conscripts all your strength and your senses for evil, in order to lead others astray and cause them to stumble through you, for he is wicked and exploits everyone who submits to him and walks in his way.

entries.section: (3) The welcome of the lands for Holofernes and his destruction of them

paragraphs.text: Pipes: plural of the pipe, a wind musical instrument.

The inhabitants of those lands tried to appease Holofernes, so their leaders came out with garlands of flowers, lamps and musical instruments, such as drums and pipes, welcoming him as a great ruler who would lead their lands and govern them in peace, hoping by this to win his kindness.

entries.section: (3) The welcome of the lands for Holofernes and his destruction of them

paragraphs.text: Unfortunately these peoples found nothing but cruelty, and he insisted on destroying not only their cities but also their fields and their forests, so that no source of life would remain to them, because the king's command was strict that he alone should be the only god of all these peoples. So he destroyed their temples and the sacred groves in which they held their worship, so that they would worship no god but Nabuchodonosor. This shows the extent of the domination and violence in Holofernes, for he did not want to take possession of their bodies, their cities and their property only, but also of their souls, so that they would submit to the worship of the king alone.

You cannot make peace with the devil or appease him, for he is determined to destroy your life. The one who offers you the pleasure of lust at the beginning suddenly turns into a mighty giant who wants to destroy your life, because he desires to be your god instead of God, and to dominate your soul, indeed all souls.

entries.section: (3) The welcome of the lands for Holofernes and his destruction of them

paragraphs.text: Syria of Sobal and Bamia: anciently called Aram, it lies west of the river Euphrates and was a strong kingdom at that time.
The Edomites: they dwelt in Mount Seir and are the descendants of Esau. These mountains lie south of the land of the Jews and extend from the south of the Dead Sea to the regions of Egypt.

Among the lands that Holofernes took possession of were the lands of Syria (the Levant) and the land of the Edomites, and he rested there for a month in a city called Geba, where he reorganized the ranks of his army and arranged its needs, in preparation for continuing his sweep and his conquest of the lands of the world.

I wish that you would examine yourself, in order to rearrange your life every day and every month, so that you renew your covenants with God, ask for His help and be strengthened with your spiritual weapons, and so defeat your enemies the demons.

The readiness of the Jews to fight the Assyrians. After the first three chapters displayed the power of the Assyrian army and its sweep through all the lands of the world, chapters 4-7 show the faith of the people of God, the power that is with them, and their readiness to face this great army, as a preparation for triumphing over it.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for war

paragraphs.text: Their loins: the plural of the loin, the muscle of man's chest, which trembles when he is afraid.

When the Jews who dwelt in the southern kingdom, that is, the land of Judah, whose capital is Jerusalem, where the great temple of God is, heard and learned the news of the army of Holofernes and its sweep through all the cities through which it passed and its destruction of their gods, they feared that he would attack the temple of Jerusalem and destroy it, and they also feared for themselves. This is the feeling of the ordinary human being at the horror of terrifying news.

It is beautiful that they feared for the temple of God, for this shows their love and their attachment to God's dwelling in their midst and their bond with Him, although this fear of theirs shows the weakness of their faith, because God is able to defend His temple if they hold fast to Him.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for war

paragraphs.text: Samaria: the region of Samaria extends from Judea in the south to Galilee in the north, and from the river Jordan in the east to near the Mediterranean Sea in the west. In this region lies the city of Samaria, which was the capital of the northern kingdom of the Jews until the days of the Assyrian attack with which we are dealing. This city lies northwest of Shechem at a distance of five and a half miles.

Jericho: a great city, five miles west of the river Jordan and seventeen miles northeast of Jerusalem. It was the first city that Joshua took possession of when he entered the land of Canaan after crossing the Jordan.

Eliakim, the high priest who dwelt in Jerusalem (v. 5), was considered at this time the civil head, because King Manasseh was imprisoned in Babylon for a short period. Eliakim is Joakim, who sent messages to the whole region of Samaria as far as Jericho in the south when he sensed the approach of the Assyrian army, so that they would prepare for war and place guards on the tops of the mountains to watch the armies coming from afar, because the one on the top of the mountain can easily strike with arrows anyone who approaches the foot of the mountain.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for war

paragraphs.text: To complete the preparations for war, the children of Israel took care to make walls for the villages that had no walls, because the cities and some of the villages had strong walls. They also took care to gather the harvest of wheat and other grains, such as barley, and stored it in the cities, so that if any city was besieged there would be food inside enough for the people for a long time.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for war

paragraphs.text: Esdraelon: a plain, or a great triangular valley, whose base is at the river Jordan and whose tip extends to near the Mediterranean Sea; it lies north of Samaria and south of Galilee.
The great plain: most likely the desert of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Saudi Arabia, which lies east of the river Jordan.
Dothan: a region located northwest of the plain of Esdraelon, that is, toward the Mediterranean.
Over against: opposite, or toward.
Ascents: summits.
The passages: narrow paths between the mountains, which sometimes admit only one person, or two.

The high priest Eliakim sent in particular to the lands surrounding the plain of Esdraelon and lying on the roads leading to Jerusalem, that they should be strict in guarding the tops of the mountains with trained soldiers, and likewise should guard the passages that lie between the mountains, and thus prevent the passage of any army trying to reach the holy city Jerusalem, in which the temple of God is.

entries.section: (1) Preparation for war

paragraphs.text: The leaders of the cities and villages and all the people obeyed the commands of the high priest and carried out all his instructions.

It is important in the spiritual warfare that a person exert all his effort in guarding his thoughts and his senses, and in closing every gap through which the devil can enter, and in caring for his spiritual food, and in arming himself with all the spiritual weapons: prayers, fasts and spiritual readings, especially in the places and circumstances in which an attack from the devil is expected, relying on his basic spiritual food, that is, partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

entries.section: (2) Spiritual preparation

paragraphs.text: Supplication: prayer.

Alongside the preparation for war, the more important thing was the spiritual work, so the whole people came forward not only with prayers but with crying and supplications to God, joined with fasting, to humble themselves before God in lowliness, asking for His help and His mercy. Women took part in these prayers with the men, that is, the people in all their groups, that God might protect them.

entries.section: (2) Spiritual preparation

paragraphs.text: Sackcloth: coarse garments suited to austerity and humbling oneself before God. It was made of camel's hair or goat's hair, dark in color, and was worn either under the outer garments or over them, as a declaration of grief and humility before God.

The priests led the people in humbling themselves before God in prayer; they put on sackcloth, and so did the rest of the people, that is, they put aside the wearing of splendor, because of their sense of their weakness and to show their humility before God.

The people cast their children down before the temple of the Lord, declaring their inability to protect them and asking for His mercy and His deliverance of them and their children. Then we find an act we hear of for the first time, declaring the extent of grief and humility before God, when the priests covered the altar of bronze with sackcloth, offering their supplications and humility, they and their altar and all their sacrifices, seeking through them the mercy of God.

entries.section: (2) Spiritual preparation

paragraphs.text: All the people and their leaders took part in praying and crying out to God, that He might have mercy on them and deliver their children, because they were weak, and likewise their women, from being seized by the enemies, who would divide them among themselves to lie with them. They also asked for the deliverance of their cities from the ruin of the enemies, and they made supplication above all for their holy temple, that the enemies might not enter it and defile it, and that God might protect them from shame and mockery among the nations, but lift them up and glorify them. This shows the extent of their faith in the power of God and at the same time their humility and their sense of their great need of the delivering hand of God. They differ from the rest of the nations, which feared Holofernes and surrendered in despair, because the fear of the Jews drove them in faith to make supplication to God and ask for His help, and they also did their duty in the preparation for war according to the commands of the high priest, so that in the end they obtained the power of God supporting them, as will appear in the following chapters.

The hour of affliction is the strongest moment in which fervent prayers go forth, in which a person humbles himself before God and casts all his hope upon Him, so that he feels the presence of God with him and enjoys His care.

entries.section: (3) The encouragement of the high priest

paragraphs.text: Eliakim felt his responsibility for his people, as their spiritual and civil leader, so he went about through the lands of the children of Israel to encourage them to prepare and to face the enemies with faith.

entries.section: (3) The encouragement of the high priest

paragraphs.text: He assured them that God would surely answer their requests if they persevered in their striving and their prayers, not because God does not hear them, but because their persistence shows their faith and their clinging to God and draws out His mercies.

entries.section: (3) The encouragement of the high priest

paragraphs.text: He reminded them of the power of God who dwells in their midst, who had strengthened Moses the chief of the prophets in ancient times when he faced his enemies the Amalekites, who relied on their strength and their weapons, and defeated them, not with more weapons than those the people had, but by his prayers which he raised on the mountain, so that Joshua the commander of the army was able to defeat them, and God showed by this that it was His power that overcame the enemies and not the power of His people (Ex 17:8-13).

entries.section: (3) The encouragement of the high priest

paragraphs.text: If God defeated the Amalekites, then you understand, O people of God, that He is able to defeat all enemies however great their strength, on condition that the people continue in their faith and their prayers. Thus, by practical proofs, Eliakim encouraged his people, so that they would not be dismayed at the power of the enemies and the submission of all to them.

Here the importance of the work of the servant appears, indeed the responsibility of each one of us in encouraging others and supporting them in their spiritual striving, whether with our brethren or our children, however great their apparent weakness or the strength of the problems that meet them. For God, who strengthened our holy fathers, is able to support us in all our steps, that we may triumph over all the wars of the devil, and prosper in everything our hands reach out to.

entries.section: (3) The encouragement of the high priest

paragraphs.text: The people took courage, so they continued in prayer before the temple of the Lord and in every place, with supplications and faith in His power, leaving aside their comfort and their material needs in order to hold fast to fervent prayers before God.

entries.section: (3) The encouragement of the high priest

paragraphs.text: The people came forward with repentance and many prayers, and offered sacrifices to God that He might have mercy on them. The priests and the Levites who offered the sacrifices did so in humility and with many prayers, wearing sackcloth and beseeching God to have mercy on them; indeed, to carry their humility further they put ashes on their heads, to declare that they were dust and ashes before God and that He was their only strength.

entries.section: (3) The encouragement of the high priest

paragraphs.text: In sum, all were asking God to intervene, that He might preserve His people and protect them from the enemies and never leave them, because of their need of Him.

Perseverance in spiritual striving confirms our clinging to God and brings us His mercies, because perseverance is proof of our sonship, so we enjoy the care of God – our spiritual Father – and He brings us out of all our troubles. So we are not troubled if the spiritual striving is prolonged, for victory is guaranteed to us by God as long as we hold fast to Him.
We see in this chapter specific steps by which the people prepared for war, that is, their fear turned into practical striving, as follows:
1- They built walls for the villages (v. 4).
2- They gathered wheat in the cities (v. 4).
3- They secured the ascents of the mountains (v. 6).
4- They guarded the passages between the mountains (v. 6).
5- They prayed to God with crying and supplication (v. 8).
6- They fasted (v. 8).
7- They humbled themselves by wearing sackcloth, the priests and the people and even the altar (v. 9).
8- They cast their children down before God (v. 9).
9- They asked for their women to be delivered from being seized (v. 10).
10- They asked for the protection of their cities and their temple from ruin and defilement for the sake of the glory of God, so that they would not become a reproach (v. 10).
11- The high priest went about encouraging the people and reminding them of the power of God which was with the fathers and that it would be with them (v. 11).
12- They continued in prayers before God (v. 15).
13- The priests and the Levites humbled themselves by putting ashes on their heads (v. 16). Achior informs Holofernes of the power of the children of Israel

entries.section: (1) Holofernes inquires about the strength of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Was enraged: was angry with violent fury.
His indignation: his rage.
Moab: the descendants of Lot, a people neighboring the children of Israel, dwelling on the eastern bank of the river Jordan, who were at odds with the children of Israel most of the time.

The children of Ammon: also descendants of Lot, dwelling beside the children of Israel, east of the Dead Sea and south of Moab. They too were at odds with the children of Israel, like the children of Moab.

The news of the preparations of the children of Israel for war reached Holofernes – the commander of the Assyrian armies – through his spies, whom he had sent ahead of him everywhere. He became very angry, because he had not expected anyone to try to fight him, as a result of his extreme pride and his earlier victories, which made him despise all the nations of the world and their gods. But at the same time he was disturbed, and with his military experience he began to gather information about the children of Israel. He found no better source than their neighbors, whose lands he had taken and who had surrendered to him, to ask them about the children of Israel. The most important of these were the peoples of Moab and the children of Ammon, who dwell east of the Jordan, opposite the land of the Jews and the plain of Esdraelon, which lies west of the Jordan (ch. 4:5).

entries.section: (1) Holofernes inquires about the strength of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: They gathered for Holofernes the military leaders of Moab and the children of Ammon, and they stood before him. Holofernes, in extreme anger and rage, asked them, inquiring about the military strength of the children of Israel, and demanded details about their cities and how well fortified they were, the strength of their armies, their numbers, and the commander of their armies. Then he asked in disapproval and astonishment how they had made light of his great army and had not submitted to him like the rest of the lands of the world, but had prepared to fight him!

So the devil always makes light of the children of God in their apparent weakness, forgetting the power of God hidden in them, as Goliath made light of David, but was killed by his hands, and as Satan made light of saints such as St. George and St. Anthony, but was defeated by them.

Do not take the outward, superficial view, for the small and weak may be mighty because God is with him, and on the contrary the great and mighty may be weak because God has left him. Do not make light of yourself however weak you may be, but prepare to fight the devil and be confident that you are able to triumph over him, however great his power and the power of his wicked helpers.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Achior: the supreme commander of all the armies of the children of Ammon; the meaning of his name is brother of light.

Achior came forward courageously from among the commanders of the armies of Moab and the children of Ammon and stood before Holofernes, and declared with great humility his readiness to tell him all the truth about the children of Israel who dwell in the mountains and about their strength.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The Chaldeans: the inhabitants of Chaldea, which lies south of Babylon; they are the original inhabitants of the region of Mesopotamia.
Mesopotamia: between the rivers Tigris and Euphrates, which lie in the present country of Iraq. Ways: laws and forms of worship.

Achior told Holofernes that the origin of the children of Israel was the Chaldeans, who dwell in Mesopotamia. They are the descendants of Abraham, and they left the pagan gods and all the worship and rites connected with them, and believed in God the Creator of heaven and earth and worshiped Him.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The God of heaven: a name of the God of the children of Israel, by which He was known anciently among the nations.

Achior recounted the history of the children of Israel briefly, speaking of Abraham and his seed in the plural, that is, that they are the people of God who left their original land according to God's command, then went down to Egypt and multiplied there. Abraham worshiped God while he was in Mesopotamia, in Ur of the Chaldeans, and offered Him worship of prostration and prayers. Then God commanded him to leave his land and go to Canaan. He passed first through Haran in the north of Mesopotamia and dwelt in it until his father Terah died, then went to Canaan and stayed in it until he died, then his son Isaac, and after him his grandson Jacob. When the famine spread over all the world, Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt, and Joseph his son, who was ruler over Egypt, received them as guests, and they multiplied there for about four hundred years, until their number reached about two million, so that they were like a great army because of their numbers.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Dealt hardly with them: was severe in his treatment of them and multiplied hardships upon them.

Clay and brick: brick is the unbaked block, and clay is what binds the bricks together. Later, building developed, so they came to burn the bricks, which became red brick, and instead of using clay they now use cement.

When the number of the children of Israel increased in Egypt, the king feared them and was severe in his treatment of them and made them labor at building cities and humbled them greatly. They cried out to their God, who intervened and struck Egypt by the hand of Moses with the ten plagues, so that Pharaoh of Egypt might submit and allow the children of Israel to go out from him.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Their rear: that is, those who were waiting for them from their families in Egypt, whom they left behind them when they went out to pursue the children of Israel.
Depth: bottom.
Dry land: what is meant is the land, that is, the solid ground found on the floor of the sea.

The tenth plague with which God struck Egypt was the hardest of the plagues, for in it all the firstborn in Egypt were struck, so Pharaoh was compelled in fear to let the people of the children of Israel go. But after their departure he felt that he had lost a great number of workers who had been helping him for nothing, so he went out after them to bring them back to Egypt by force. The children of Israel had reached the Red Sea, and God divided the sea for them, so that the waters became like a wall on both sides, and the children of Israel crossed on the ground at the bottom of the sea. Even so the Egyptians were not afraid, but pursued them. After the children of Israel came out of the sea, Moses struck the sea, and Pharaoh and all the army of the Egyptians were drowned, and not one of them remained to tell those who dwelt in Egypt what had happened to them; rather, the news of this great event spread and reached Egypt.

This is the power of God in His children who obey Him: even if He lets them endure many afflictions, He returns and saves them with a great power that no one expects. So be patient, my brother, in affliction, obeying the commandments of God, confident that He will lift from you all your troubles and humble for you all the demons that fight you, so that you are assured of complete victory over them.

You must be estranged from the world and leave your family and your kindred like Abraham, then accept affliction in the land of Egypt, and then God appears and makes your enemies afraid. Then you pass through the sea, that is, in Baptism, and die with Christ and rise with Him, and by that you triumph. In every repentance, confession and Communion you experience that victory, and your striving is completed when you pass over this world and rise with Christ on the last day.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Then God's care for His children appears in the midst of afflictions and hard circumstances that cannot be borne. In the barren wilderness of Sinai, where an ordinary person cannot live, two million human beings lived under the care of God.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: In the wilderness of Sinai the children of Israel found no water to drink, so God turned the bitter water into sweet water for them; and they found no food, so He sent down manna for them from heaven. And for forty years God continued to sustain them and give them their food and drink in the wilderness.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Shield: a piece of wood usually covered with leather, with a loop behind it into which the soldier puts his hand. This shield is used to protect his head and body from the arrows aimed at him.

The people of God in the wilderness of Sinai were exposed to attack by enemies, such as the Amalekites, who were strong men of huge bodies. They triumphed over them easily by the power of God and not by weapons of war, which have no strength against the power of these enemies.

Therefore let my heart be at rest, because "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want": He supplies my needs in the midst of afflictions and fights for me against my enemies the demons, so that I rise from my sins and triumph over them and rejoice at all times.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel remained strong, and none could overcome them unless they abandoned the worship of God; then their shame and weakness appeared and their enemies triumphed over them. This happened often in the age of the Judges, when the people worshiped the idols of the nations around them and intermarried with them, so these lands rose against them and occupied them and humbled them and plundered their spoil and possessions, as is clear in the Book of Judges.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, the Hittites, the Hivites and the Amorites: the peoples who dwelt east and west of the river Jordan, whom Joshua triumphed over and whose lands he possessed.

Heshbon: a city of Moabite origin, in which King Sihon the Amorite reigned, lying east of the river Jordan between the rivers Arnon and Jabbok. Moses took possession of it and gave it to the tribe of Reuben. If the children of Israel repent of their sins and return to God and worship Him, He gives them power to overcome all their enemies, as happened after their defeat before Ai in the days of Joshua, when they repented and triumphed over the kings of the land of Canaan and occupied their lands, and as David and Solomon triumphed and subdued the peoples around them, as is mentioned in the books of First and Second Samuel and First Kings.
They kept their strength and God's dwelling in their midst as long as they held fast to His commandments and His worship and kept far from evil, because their God hates evil.

entries.section: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Achior gave an example to confirm his words: when the people of God departed from His worship and worshiped idols, they became weak, so the Assyrians overcame them and took possession of their lands, and even reached their capital Jerusalem – in the days of King Manasseh – and seized him, and of course took many of the leaders and men of war from Jerusalem and carried them to Babylon, and they remained there until Manasseh repented in the prison of Babylon, and God had mercy on him and brought him back, with those of his people who had been taken captive, to Jerusalem and the mountains of Judea, and they possessed them again (2 Chr 33:11-13).

I wish, my brother, that you would be confident that it is sin that makes us lose the care and fatherhood of God. So let us hold fast to His commandments and repent of our sins, and He will forgive them for us in the sacraments of confession and Communion, and we will enjoy His protection and His power working in us.

entries.section: (3) The advice of Achior and the anger of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Yoke: a crosswise piece of wood from the middle of which another piece of wood projects at right angles, to the end of which the agricultural implement is attached; the crosswise piece is placed on the necks of two animals that draw this implement. The yoke is a symbol of domination, and what is meant here is the power of authority and the control and enslavement of the people by Holofernes. We are not able to withstand them: we cannot face them, because they are much stronger than we.
Achior gave Holofernes clear and sincere guidance about his plan of war for fighting the children of Israel, drawn from the facts he had recounted about them, which are summarized as follows:
1- No one can resist the power of the God of the children of Israel; rather, he becomes a reproach and a shame before Him.
2- God does not leave His people unless they sin, and then they become weak and can be overcome.

3- Their condition must be learned: if they have fallen into sin and God is angry with them, they are without strength and can be fought and overcome. But if they worship Him faithfully and uprightly, let us keep away from them, because their strength surpasses every power on earth.
If others know the power of our God that is in us and bear witness to it, shall we not hold fast to our faith and trust in our God, and not be terrified by the powers of the world?

entries.section: (3) The advice of Achior and the anger of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: When the commanders of the armies, the assistants of Holofernes, who were standing in his presence, heard the words of Achior, they were very angry, for it was the first time they had heard of a power that could stand before them. They were drowned in pride, thinking they were the strongest power in the world, and they made light of the children of Israel, since their number was small and their military experience weak, and therefore – in their view – their God was weak before Nabuchodonosor, whom they thought to be the strongest god in the world, and they were trying to prove this. So they felt that Achior was loyal to the children of Israel and deceiving Holofernes, and they tried to kill him for his boldness in saying these words, declaring the power of the children of Israel and their God.

entries.section: (3) The advice of Achior and the anger of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Given up to the sword: deserving to be killed by the sword.

Despite the rage of the men of Holofernes and their desire to kill Achior, they postponed it until they should take possession of the land of the Jews and destroy it and kill those in it, with Achior among them, in order to declare to the whole world that the strongest god in the world is Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians.

So the pride of man makes him forget the power of God and reject any testimony to Him. I wish that you would not reject the opinions of others that God may send to you to bear witness to Him, or to call you to humility and repentance. Achior is not a deceiver but a witness to God. Look, lest God has sent you an Achior in your wife, or your husband, or your father, or your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or your friend, or any person around you, and you reject his words in pride, that is, the voice of God sent to you. The voice may be very clear and supported with proofs, like the words of Achior, and you reject it as you reject the words of the Holy Bible, the guidance of your father of confession and the teachings of the Church, and then you go further in boldness, rebuking and insulting the one who declares to you the voice of God, even trying to kill him, that is, to silence the voice of God, so that you may remain in your sin.
Achior in Bethulia

entries.section: (1) The delivering of Achior to the Jews

paragraphs.text: Prophesied: the words of Achior that appear as a prophecy are with God's help, to declare the truth before Holofernes, that perhaps he might fear God, otherwise divine punishment would come upon him. For God gives an opportunity for repentance to all people, even the wicked. After the men of Holofernes were angered by the words of Achior, thinking that he was an agent of the children of Israel and a deceiver of the Assyrians, the great anger of Holofernes then appeared, and he spoke with Achior the commander of the armies of the children of Ammon. He spoke in all pride, declaring the facts that would happen as he saw them: that the army of the Assyrians would strike the children of Israel as if they were striking one man, and by this their weakness and the weakness of their God would appear, like the rest of the gods of the nations, and it would then appear that the only god in the world is Nabuchodonosor; and then the Assyrians would kill Achior with them, and he would have only a little life left, so that he might see with his own eyes the death of the children of Israel with him. Holofernes, the commander of the Assyrian armies, continued his speech to Achior with all confidence, saying to him: Why are you in alarm and fear of this fate? For if your prophecy and your faith in what you said about the power of the God of Israel are true, no harm will come to you. The remarkable thing here is that Achior the Gentile did not have his faith shaken, but remained more confident in the power of the God of heaven than in the power of the armies of the Assyrians.

entries.section: (1) The delivering of Achior to the Jews

paragraphs.text: The sword of my army shall pierce your sides: one of the means of torture is that a person dies with the sword piercing his sides, that is, he dies a slow death, and is tormented, instead of having his head cut off, so that he dies and finds rest quickly. This method was used by the pagans and taken from them by the Jews (2 Sam 2:16), and it is a means that warriors use to frighten their enemies and to encourage themselves to destroy them.
Until: that is, after a very short period of time, counted in minutes.

Holofernes declared in anger to Achior that when he dies and is tormented with the sword piercing his forehead, he will be certain, by experiencing this torment, that there is no god in all the earth except Nabuchodonosor, by whose army's sword Achior will die. All this Achior will know as he breathes his last, with the Jews lying dead around him.

entries.section: (1) The delivering of Achior to the Jews

paragraphs.text: Holofernes continued his speech in pride, trying to plant fear in the heart of Achior, and said to him, why are you in alarm, so that your face has turned pale? Yet this did not happen, and Achior remained in his faith in the help of God, but the pride of Holofernes blinded his eyes, and made him imagine that Achior was in great fear.

So the devil always speaks with all confidence, as if he were reciting facts and conclusions that must be, to make us doubt the power of our God that protects us, and to make us fall into distress, alarm and despair, so that we forget that he is the liar and the father of lies. Hold fast, my brother, to your faith, however great the apparent power of the world may seem, for all the gods of the world and its powers are nothing before the power of your God. Declare your faith, confident that all the threats of the world are vain, and even if you are alone like Achior among the wicked who threaten you, you are stronger than they by the power of your God. If the faith of Achior the Gentile was like this, how much more should your faith be!

entries.section: (1) The delivering of Achior to the Jews

paragraphs.text: Then Holofernes issued his decree to seize Achior and deliver him to the people of Israel, so that he would die with them when the Assyrians attacked them.

entries.section: (1) The delivering of Achior to the Jews

paragraphs.text: Bethulia: a small city located north of the region of Samaria and northwest of the plain of Esdraelon.

It is thus on the northern front facing the invaders, who wanted to take possession of the land of the Jews in the region of Samaria, then the region of Judea, in which Jerusalem lies and in which is the temple of God. So the men of Holofernes seized Achior and went with him toward the city of Bethulia, in which the children of Israel dwell, which is built on a mountain.

entries.section: (1) The delivering of Achior to the Jews

paragraphs.text: Drew near: came close.
Slings: plural of the sling, a simple weapon of war.

When the servants of Holofernes drew near the mountain on which the city of Bethulia stands, the men of war defending the city came out throwing stones with slings, for they thought that the servants of Holofernes were the vanguard of his army trying to attack the city.

entries.section: (1) The delivering of Achior to the Jews

paragraphs.text: Under the vengeance: when vengeance comes upon them.

So the Assyrians hurried to the side of the mountain to get out of range of the stones, lest they hit them, and they found a tree, and tied Achior to it and left him bound, and went back to Holofernes.

The devil, whom Holofernes signifies, in the extremity of his evil and his causing doubt in believers, leaves them to be bound to the Church – the place where believers gather – which Bethulia signifies, relying on his having bound them with the ropes of sin to the tree of material lusts; as he made Adam and Eve fall long ago by binding them with the desire to eat from the forbidden tree. Thus they are in the holy place but bound with evil lusts.

So be watchful, my brother, to the tricks of the devil, for he does not rejoice at your being in the Church among the believers and your being joined to the Holy Sacraments, but he wants to bind you with evil lusts so that you fall into sin in the holy place, and the fall is then greater.

Lift your eyes toward God, and He will loose you from the bonds of lust and give you, with the rest of the believers, the joy of fellowship with Him and His love. Be careful and attentive to the enticements of the devil at all times, even in the holy place.

entries.section: (2) Achior tells the Jews what happened with Holofernes

paragraphs.text: When the soldiers of Bethulia were certain that the servants of Holofernes did not want to attack the city, but had done a strange act, namely binding a man to a tree at the bottom of the mountain, they came down and loosed Achior from his bonds and brought him up into the midst of the city, and he stood before the elders of the city and its people gathered with them; and they asked him why the Assyrians had bound him.

entries.section: (2) Achior tells the Jews what happened with Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Ozias the son of Micah: Ozias (Uzziah) is a Hebrew word meaning the strength of God, and Micah is a Hebrew word meaning "who is like God," so that the whole of his name is the strength of God which has no like in the world. Ozias was not only one of the elders but their head, that is, the foremost head of the city and its leader, as appeared in (v. 19) when he held a feast for Achior, and also when the people protested against him and he asked them for a delay before surrendering the city (ch. 7). The tribe of Simeon: Simeon the son of Jacob, who angered God and his father when he killed, with his brother Levi, the men of the tribe of Hamor and Shechem (Gen 34). Judith also belongs to this tribe (ch. 8:1). Chabris (Karmi) the son of Gothoniel: Karmi is a Hebrew word meaning the worker in the vineyard, and Gothoniel is a Hebrew word meaning the strength of God, so the meaning of his name is "the strength of God working in the vineyard," and he is a type of Christ, who offered not only the juice of the grape but His blood on the cross.

Two rulers: that is, two foremost heads among the people, who were of the elders of the city who led it. The people chose them from among the wise and those who knew the Law, and they were usually of advanced age, to lead the people in the city as helpers to the high priest who was in Jerusalem, as we first heard of elders in the days of Moses, when his father-in-law Jethro advised him to do this to help him in judging the people (Ex 18). Achior explained to the people, and especially to the two elders, or foremost rulers, Ozias and Chabris, how he had informed Holofernes of the power of the God of Israel, the God of heaven, so that he became angry and sent him to die with the children of Israel. Two of the heads of the city, or its elders, are mentioned here: Ozias, the foremost head of the city, then Chabris, who is one of the well-known elders in it and who attended with the rest of the elders to learn the story of this man bound to a tree beside their city. These two heads are a type of Christ, the power of God and the Savior by His blood of His people.

And we see here that Ozias the head was of the tribe of Simeon, a tribe with which Jacob was angry because of its rashness in killing the tribe of Shechem, but God is able to bring strength out of weakness and to work in all His children.

entries.section: (2) Achior tells the Jews what happened with Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Achior began to explain to the elders and people of Bethulia that he was the commander of the armies of the Ammonites and that he had stood with the rest of the commanders of the armies of the surrounding lands before Holofernes, who was angry because of their readiness to fight him; and how he had made clear to him the power of the God of the Jews, who cannot be resisted as long as the people are subject to Him and keep His commandments; then how the servants of Holofernes tried to kill him because he spoke of a God stronger than Nabuchodonosor.

entries.section: (2) Achior tells the Jews what happened with Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Kinds: types.

Achior continued his speech, explaining how Holofernes commanded that he be bound and delivered to the Jews, so that he would take vengeance not only on him but on all the Jews, and Achior with them, when he attacks them and takes possession of their lands, and inflicts severe torments on Achior before he kills him.

The Jews who loosed Achior from his bonds signify the servants of the Church, who help a person to repent and be rid of the bonds of sin, and then bring him up to the Church, which the city of Bethulia, built on a mountain, signifies; for the Church is the image of heaven on earth, and the people signify the believers, the elders signify the priests, and Achior signifies the Gentiles, or those who are far off, who find their salvation in Christ within the Church when they believe in Him, so the power of God rescues them from Holofernes, who signifies Satan, and protects them within the Church.

I wish that we would rise above our worldly thoughts and the doubts of the devil and take refuge in the Church, so that all the thoughts of the enemy fall away from us, and we are strengthened by our being in the presence of Christ, among His priests and all the believers. Then our hearts take courage in the presence of the Church and its comforting, strengthening prayers.

entries.section: (3) The prayer and the comforting of Achior

paragraphs.text: Their pride: their might and haughtiness.
All: everyone.
Your saints: the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the men of God, the fathers of the people.

When the people heard the news of Holofernes and his power, and his insistence on taking vengeance on them, they took refuge quickly in God, prostrating themselves with reverence and humility before Him, and wept much, offering fervent prayers and supplications to God, declaring their weakness in great humility. They set out their problem, which was the strength of the enemies, who were fierce and very strong. But they asked God for His promises to their holy fathers, that is, they interceded by them and reminded Him of His tenderness toward the weak, for He is the strong One who helps His children in their afflictions, declaring their faith in the power of God more than in the power of the enemies, and also reminding God that He supports the weak who are humble and rejects the proud who rely on their own strength, that is, the enemies.

entries.section: (3) The prayer and the comforting of Achior

paragraphs.text: After all the people had finished their prayers, they rose reassured and joyful, for this is the natural result of true prayer offered to God. So they reassured Achior and comforted his heart that God would protect them and rescue them from the hands of Holofernes and his men.

However much the afflictions increase upon you, do not let your heart be troubled, but humble yourself and make supplication to God, confident that the power of God is displayed in the weakness of His children. Persevere in prayer even if many days pass in affliction, as the people of Bethulia persevered all day in prostration, weeping and prayer, for in the end God will comfort your heart and reassure you, and finally bring you out of all your afflictions. Seek the intercession of your beloved saints and do not be ashamed to remind God of His promises and mercies to His children, for He rejoices greatly in the prayer of His humble children; indeed, your humble prayer binds the power of Satan and keeps his harm from you.

entries.section: (3) The prayer and the comforting of Achior

paragraphs.text: Bestows this favor upon you: gives you this gift.

And the people said to Achior – perhaps this was spoken by the elders of the people such as Ozias and Chabris – that if Achior had believed in the God of Israel and had prophesied of His power, then let him be confident that he would see the salvation of God and the destruction of Holofernes and all his armies.

entries.section: (3) The prayer and the comforting of Achior

paragraphs.text: The people welcomed Achior and his household – if he should later wish to bring them – to dwell among them in Bethulia, as a Jew believing in the God of Israel, so that he would enjoy all his life the care of their God.

Stand firm in your faith in the midst of afflictions, and be confident that you will see the salvation of the Lord. Keep your place in the midst of the Church, that you may continue to enjoy God's care for you and your household all your life.

entries.section: (3) The prayer and the comforting of Achior

paragraphs.text: After the people gathered before God in prayer, they consulted the Lord, that is, they presented their problem to Him, believing in His ability to deliver them from it.

How beautiful it is that our counsel should be from God, and from His Church gathered for prayer in the form and on the tongue of her spiritual fathers. It is better than any human counsel, for the counsel of God is what protects a person and truly supports him.

entries.section: (3) The prayer and the comforting of Achior

paragraphs.text: The people departed, each to his house, to eat food after fasting all day, and all rejoiced in the comfort of God. And Ozias the head of the city called all the people again to gather and to continue praying all night, that God might intervene and rescue His people, which confirms that this was a spiritual supper, and that they were not slack in their striving to give their bodies rest.

If God comforts your heart and reassures you, it is so that you may continue your striving. Night, in the view of the people of the world, is an opportunity for laxity and idleness, even for amusement and play, but for the children of God it is an opportunity for spiritual vigil, and therefore the Church ordained the Midnight Prayer, that the night might be blessed with prayer, and ordained also the Midnight Praise (Tasbeha), that our hearts might be lifted up in praise and thanksgiving to God. Thus Satan the enemy finds us in constant spiritual wakefulness, and cannot overcome us. Night also signifies the darkness and evil of the people of the world, so we need to be watchful all the days of our life in continual prayers.
Holofernes besieges Bethulia

entries.section: (1) The advance of Holofernes upon Bethulia

paragraphs.text: The next day: after the day on which Achior was bound to the tree and delivered to Bethulia. Holofernes gave his orders to his armies to move toward Judea to fight the children of Israel, so they advanced toward Bethulia. This was on the morning of the day that the people had spent in prayer and fasting until night, so the people rested only a few hours before they saw the Assyrian advance coming against them. Perhaps this was the opposite of what the Jews expected, since they thought that God's answer would be to keep the Assyrian army away from them, but it was the wisdom of God, which will appear later.

entries.section: (1) The advance of Holofernes upon Bethulia

paragraphs.text: Footmen: the soldiers and infantry.
Those taken from the captured lands: the men whom Holofernes took captive from the lands he occupied and added to his army to fight with him.
The young men: the youths.

Holofernes gave his orders to his armies to move toward Judea to fight the children of Israel, and the great army moved, of which the Holy Bible states that the number of foot soldiers in it was one hundred and twenty thousand and the number of horsemen twenty-two thousand, in addition to several thousand soldiers who joined the army of the Assyrians from the lands Holofernes had occupied, so that the number of his army increased greatly and was hard to count, while it was not to be expected that the soldiers of the small city of Bethulia would exceed a thousand soldiers. This shows the impossibility of Bethulia triumphing over the Assyrians except by the power of God, which works miracles. It is to be noted that the number of horsemen mentioned in the text is twenty-two thousand, although the number mentioned in (ch. 2:7) is twelve thousand, but the translation of the Jesuit Fathers states in the seventh chapter that the number of horsemen is twelve thousand, so perhaps the figure of twenty-two thousand is an error in the translation we have, or in copying.

entries.section: (1) The advance of Holofernes upon Bethulia

paragraphs.text: This mighty army moved forward to Judea from the north by way of the plain of Esdraelon, which is a triangular plain lying between Galilee and Samaria, twelve miles long from north to south and twenty-five miles wide from the river Jordan to the Mediterranean Sea. Then it advanced toward a place called Cyamon, heading for the city of Bethulia, which lies on a mountain and was the first of the cities that Holofernes met when he entered Judea. His army encamped in a valley lying between Cyamon in the north and Bethulia in the south (that is, lengthwise), and in breadth it lies between Belmaim and the hill of Dothan, which overlooks its plain. In this valley the sight of the army – whose number reached tens of thousands – was fearful and mighty.

Holofernes moved with his mighty army, confident in himself that he would shatter those small lands, the first of which was Bethulia, and he did not know that there could be a power greater than he, namely the power of God, which supports the weak. Do not rely on yourself and forget God when facing problems and in your relations with others, but rely on God and have confidence in your soul that relies on Him, and you will be at peace all the days of your life.

entries.section: (1) The advance of Holofernes upon Bethulia

paragraphs.text: When the people of God in Bethulia looked from their city on the mountain at the valley before them and saw this great army, they were very afraid, so they hurried to God, prostrating themselves in reverence, and even put ashes on their heads in humility before Him, and prayed with supplication to God to have mercy on them and rescue them from the Assyrians.

entries.section: (1) The advance of Holofernes upon Bethulia

paragraphs.text: Leading: bringing.

The soldiers of Bethulia hurried to guard the places leading to the pass between the two mountains that led to the city, for it was the only entrance to the city on the mountain, and they organized an armed guard through the night and day. Thus prayers went up and were mingled with the watch; that is, they took refuge in God and did their duty at the same time.

Do not be dismayed before the multitude of the wicked, but take refuge in your God by prayer and supplication in humility and lowliness, confident in His mercies, and at the same time do your duty with all faithfulness, so that you are one who trusts in God and not one who is merely idle in reliance on Him. Guard the entrances of your heart, that is, your senses, so that evil does not enter through them, and let your spiritual wakefulness be constant night and day, and when God sees your striving He will keep you from every sin.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes cuts off the water from the city

paragraphs.text: When Holofernes saw that the city was fortified, he began to go around it to learn how to attack it. He was passing on his horse with a group of horsemen, and they found outside the city on the south the main spring of water, which supplied the city, and from which a channel came out and entered into the city. So he knew that it was the main source of the water that fed the city, and he commanded that the channel be blocked, and by this he cut off the water entering the city, that the people of Bethulia might die of thirst. The water channel emptied inside the city into a deep pit, which was considered as a reservoir of water, from which it was afterward drawn up into basins for people and animals to drink.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes cuts off the water from the city

paragraphs.text: After cutting off the water coming from the main spring that fed the city, there remained only a very few springs of water inside the city, and a few springs outside the city beside its walls. When the main source of water was cut off, the water inside the city was no longer sufficient for the needs of the people, so some of the people would go out secretly from the gates of the city and fill from these nearby springs, despite the danger of exposing themselves to the violence of the soldiers of Holofernes. Of course this water was not enough to quench the thirst of all the people, and they began to suffer from lack of water.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes cuts off the water from the city

paragraphs.text: Fence them in: surround them and protect them.
Distress: extreme affliction that is close to death.
Valleys: plural of the ravine, that is, the valley.
Impregnable: fortified.

Then the Moabites and the children of Ammon came forward, the peoples neighboring the children of Israel despite the physical kinship between them, for they are descendants of Lot, the nephew of Abraham, the father of the Jewish people, but they were hostile to them because they were pagans, whereas the Jews worshiped God. Here the cunning and craftiness of Holofernes appear in enlisting the Moabites and the Ammonites to help him in fighting the children of Israel, because they were their enemies. This was a custom known anciently in war, such as Pilate's use of the Samaritans to suppress the revolts of the Jews in Jerusalem and Judea.

When they saw Holofernes preparing to attack the city, they gloated over the Jews, and even hurried to give advice to Holofernes so that the people of Bethulia might perish. They said to him that the Jews who dwell in Bethulia rely on their city being fortified on the top of the mountain, and the mountains surround and protect it, so they do not rely for the defense of their city on the known weapons such as the sword and the spear, and you can destroy them without war by watching the springs near the walls so that they cannot draw water from them secretly.
The devil in his war with the children of God hems them in at the main sources of their livelihood, so that they fall into poverty, sickness and many troubles, hoping that they will leave God.

The wicked may also gather together when they find the children of God in calamity, to make their affliction harder by narrowing their sources of livelihood, even the secondary ones, to make sure of their destruction, and they advise their enemies to destroy them, hoping by this to win honor, or some gifts, from these enemies.

Do not fear the one who has authority to harm your body, for first, he cannot harm you unless God permits him, and only to the extent that He permits; and he also cannot touch your spirit. God permits this to see the extent of your steadfastness in the faith and your endurance of afflictions, and be confident that in the end He will give you victory over your enemies and will not permit your destruction.

Do not be dismayed when the wicked gather against you, even if they are your relatives, for they are nothing before the power of God who protects you, and even if they take from you the sources of your livelihood, God will provide for you in miraculous ways.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes cuts off the water from the city

paragraphs.text: Holofernes was pleased with their idea and set soldiers to guard these springs and kill anyone who approached them. He was strict, so he set over each spring a company of a hundred soldiers to prevent any attempt by Bethulia to draw water secretly.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes cuts off the water from the city

paragraphs.text: Their cisterns: that is, their basins, the plural of basin.

Holofernes continued his guarding of all the springs of water outside the walls of the city of Bethulia, so that only a few wells of water remained and some collections of water, that is, the basins connected to these wells. The quantity of water in them was not enough for the people, although it was distributed to each family in small measure, and after twenty days it almost dried up, and what remained of it was barely enough for one day.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: When the thirst of the people increased and they began to faint and were about to depart from life, a power to preserve their survival stirred in them, so they rose in anger in all their groups – men, women, elders and children – and seized Ozias the head of the city and began to blame him violently, because he refused to come to terms with the Assyrians and surrender the city to them. Their sense of their life slipping away from them made them forget their faith in God and their love for Ozias the head of their city, so they rebuked him severely, ascribing the fault to him, although they had been convinced of the preparation for war, the fervent prayer and the tears they had poured out before God. But all this collapsed before the confrontation with death.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Helper: a support and deliverer.
Be struck down: die.

The people expressed their condition by saying that they were dying slowly of thirst, and having lost their faith in God, they said that they had no one to rescue them and support them in their trial.
