When affliction grows severe upon you, instead of falling into despair and anger at others and directing accusations at them, I wish that you would hasten and cast your troubles at the feet of Christ, for He feels for you, and is nearer to you than at any other time, and is ready to help you.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Facing the fear of death, the foremost of the people asked Ozias to call everyone in the city to go out to Holofernes and surrender themselves to him, so that they would become slaves and captives, in order to escape death.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: The people felt that surrendering themselves to Holofernes would give them life, and that this was better, because life is better than death, since they could worship God and bless Him with many prayers while alive, but if they remained in the city they would die and lose their ability to pray, and would be tormented by seeing their children and women die before their eyes, and in the end they themselves would die also. How cruel death is, for facing death is hard. When a person feels death creeping up to master him, he is greatly disturbed, especially if he sees with his own eyes the death of his children, for they are dearer to him than himself, so he defends them out of the instinct of motherhood or fatherhood, to the point that some people rush to kill their children so as not to see them die before their eyes.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Our end: the end of our life.
The burning of thirst: very severe thirst.

Then they pressed Ozias and the elders of the city and tried to extract from them a promise and an oath to surrender the city and those in it to Holofernes, and they declared that they were sinners and that the affliction that came upon them was divine discipline. They even said that quick death by the sword at the hand of Holofernes was better than dying of thirst, because quick death by the sword does not torment a person like slow death by thirst; that is, they were determined in every case to surrender themselves to the Assyrians, whether they spared their lives or killed them. This shows the extent of their despair and the weakness of their faith.

I wish that affliction would lead us to hold fast to God, and that according to our attachment to the spiritual life we would endure material afflictions and remain steadfast in our faith, not accepting slavery to sin or delivering our life to Satan, for to die while we are pure and free from sin is better than to live while we are drowned in evils.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Wailing: weeping with a loud voice.
Fainted: fell to the ground in extreme exhaustion.
Were weary: grew tired.

From the despair of the people and the difficulty of their facing death by thirst, they showed their distress with Ozias and accused him of being the cause of their destruction and demanded that he surrender the city. But their faith was still alive, though weak, so they took refuge in God, their only refuge, with prayer, crying and tears for long hours, and they even offered common prayers with one voice, showing the oneness of their feelings. The following appeared in their prayers:

1- Their repentance and their confession of their faults and the faults of their fathers. Repentance is the first thing by which we draw out the mercies of God. Their remembrance of the sins of their fathers goes back to a mistaken belief that was prevalent among the Jews, that children are punished because of the sins of their fathers, but God made clear the error of this belief in (Ex 18:2-4).
2- Their hoping for the mercies of God to rescue them from their enemies.

3- Since their faults deserve punishment, if God sees fit to punish them, let Him punish them Himself and not deliver them into the hands of their enemies. Here they imitate David the prophet who said, "Let us fall now into the hand of the Lord; for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man" (2 Sam 24:14).

4- Their asking that God would rescue them and be glorified in them, so that the power of God would appear before all the peoples, instead of its being said that God had left them if Holofernes stormed them. From the abundance of their crying and prayers they grew weary and in the end fell silent, with their hearts speaking instead of their lips, and they waited for the mercies of God and His help. Thus by repentance, faith and prayers to God, putting their hope in Him and not in the pagan gods, they were able to draw out the mercies of God, and they offered complete striving unto death.

I wish that we would take refuge in God before everything, because none other than He loves us and is able to save us. And as long as we come before Him with repentance and humility, we shall surely obtain His mercies, even if He permits our punishment, for He is merciful and does not leave us to perish, and in the end the name of God is glorified in us.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Finally Ozias spoke, the head of the city and the one responsible for leading this people.

Here wise leadership appears: he was not disturbed by their accusation of him, nor angry with them, but shared their feelings, their prayers, their crying and their tears, and felt his responsibility, so he stood with them to reassure them of the presence of God. Then he took a spiritual decision better than what they had asked, for he asked them to wait five days, in prayers, to see God's intervention and His deliverance of them, instead of surrendering the city at once as they asked. And if God did not intervene, then after five days he would surrender the city.

Perhaps he asked their permission to wait five days because he knew that the small quantity of water in the city could suffice for them for five days, and by this the extent of Ozias' holding to endurance appears, to the utmost that the people could bear. It is striving unto death, that is, to the utmost possible striving, as the New Testament teaches us to strive unto blood (Heb 12:4)

How beautiful it is that you bear your responsibility, whether as the head of a family, or as a servant in the Church, or as one responsible in any work, so that you care for those with you and bear with their faults and encourage them and guide them spiritually. Care also for your own spiritual life, so that your spiritual stature and your faith may grow, and you may be able to carry out the tasks of your service and your responsibility. According to the spiritual stature of the servant he is able to guide and lead his people spiritually.

It is evident that Ozias had a spiritual stature greater than his people. Though a greater spiritual stature will appear afterward in Judith, not only than the people, but than all the elders of the city and than Ozias himself.
The faith of Judith and her rebuke of the elders (1) The character of Judith (vv. 1-8:)

1- And when Judith the widow heard these words, who was the daughter of Merari the son of Idus, the son of Joseph, the son of Ozias, the son of Elai, the son of Minor, the son of Gideon, the son of Raphaim, the son of Ahitub, the son of Malchiah, the son of Hanan, the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Mashon, the son of Reuben. 2- And her husband was Manasseh, and he died in the days of the barley harvest. 3- For as he stood over those that bound the sheaves in the field, the heat struck his head, and he died in Bethulia his city, and was buried there with his fathers. 4- And Judith had remained a widow three years and six months. 5- And she had prepared for herself a secret chamber at the top of her house, and she dwelt in it with her maidservants and kept it shut. 6- And she had sackcloth upon her loins, and she fasted all the days of her life, except the sabbaths and the new moons and the feasts of the house of Israel. 7- And she was of a very beautiful countenance, and her husband had left her great riches and many servants and possessions full of herds of oxen and flocks of sheep. 8- And she had a good report among all people, because she feared the Lord greatly, and there was none that spoke an ill word of her.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: The Holy Bible presents us here with the person of Judith – the meaning of which is "Jewess" – and tells us of her lineage. She was from the tribe of Simeon, as is confirmed at the beginning of the ninth chapter (ch. 9:2-3). She speaks of her father Simeon, of whom his father Jacob said that he was wrathful, and in his anger he and Levi rose up because of Shechem's assault on their sister, and they rose and killed all the men of the city (Gen 49:5-7). She is proud of belonging to Simeon, who was distinguished for courage, and she does not mean his rashness and impetuosity, for Judith was courageous like her ancestor Simeon. As for the mention of Reuben, it may be because he was considered the firstborn of Jacob; and in the Jesuit translation of this book the name of Reuben is not mentioned.

It is to be noted that Judith's descent is traced back to her ancestor Simeon and includes fifteen generations, because the Jews – until the birth of Christ – took care of their genealogies, so that God might declare the fulfillment of His promise that Christ would come from the seed of David and from the seed of Judah.

Among the graces of God is that this great woman – as will become clear from what follows – did not live beside the temple in Jerusalem, but in the northern kingdom of the Jews, whose capital is Samaria, where the worship of idols was widespread, and yet she remained holding fast to her faith; indeed her faith was very strong, as appears also in the person of the great Tobit in his love and his faith, who was also from the northern kingdom. For God is able to keep you and to develop your faith however bad the circumstances around you, if you continue to hold fast to Him.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Urged on: encourages and motivates the workers to work energetically.
Struck: that is, scorched; the meaning is that his temperature rose as a result of the intense heat of the sun on his head.

Judith married and her husband died – as it seems – at a young age, a short time after her marriage, for Manasseh her husband was working energetically in the field during the harvest, making light of the fatigue because he was young, and the intense heat struck him and he died. As a rich man and an owner of possessions he used to urge on the workers in his fields to complete the harvest, and the sun struck him, because the barley harvest is in about the month of May and the heat then is intense.
Sunstroke in ancient times was difficult to treat and ended a person's life, as happened with the son of the Shunammite woman, the widow, whom Elisha the prophet raised (2 Kgs 4:18-20).

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: After the death of Judith's husband she kept to her widowhood, although she was young and very beautiful and rich, and this is a proof of her chastity.

Her husband died and she accepted the affliction as an opportunity to live with God. She represents the human soul that accepts God's dispensations with thanksgiving, and even seizes affliction to draw near to God and consecrate her heart to Him.

The period of three and a half years is that in which Elijah shut up heaven, that the people might repent and return to God, and after this the heavy rain came down (Jas 5). It also signifies the period of affliction at the end of the days, of which the Book of Revelation tells us (Rev 12), which the children of God endure, or the three and a half days in which the bodies of the two prophets lie in the street of the great city, and then rise (Rev 11), of which Daniel prophesied (Dan 12). So after a widowhood of three and a half years, Judith rejoiced in the salvation of God by her hands for all her people, and Holofernes, who signifies Satan, died, and all his soldiers were defeated. For the period of three and a half years signifies the temporary afflictions that we endure in life, after which the crisis is relieved.

Judith did not need to marry her husband's brother – as the Law requires – because she desired virginity, and God helped her in that by widowhood. So she lived all her life worshiping God in chastity and asceticism, like Anna the prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel (Lk 2:36-38).

Truly all things work together for good to them that love God (Rom 8:28). God manages your life even if you do not understand; He permits affliction so that He may be glorified in it and work in weakness more than in human strength, as the Apostle Paul said, "When I am weak, then am I strong" (2 Cor 12:10).

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Her loins: the middle and below, the region of the body that the undergarments cover.
Sackcloth: a coarse garment resembling burlap.
New moons: the Jews used to keep a feast at the beginning of the months.
Household: the private servants and maidservants whom she owned.

The Holy Bible testifies that Judith was very rich, and even describes her many possessions of herds of oxen and flocks of sheep, and yet she left behind all these many comforts and left behind what every woman cares about, namely her beauty, although she possessed wonderful beauty. And strangely, she also gave up the enjoyment of her great mansion and lived in an upper room, to live a life of solitude in many prayers and acts of worship.
Thus she lived voluntary poverty, and she is a clear example from the Old Testament of the importance of solitude and seclusion, which appeared as the system of monasticism in the New Testament.

It is worth pointing out the good influence of Judith on her maidservants who worked in her house, for they too came to love prayer and worship, so her upper room became a house for virgins. Perhaps St. Demiana and the forty virgins followed her example when they lived in the palace that Marcus the governor built for his daughter Demiana. She was distinguished in her solitude by severe asceticism, for she left behind the soft garments of the rich and put on sackcloth, that is, coarse garments, as an application of severe austerity, and she fasted all the year, except the festal days of the liturgical calendar that the Law prescribes.
And when Judith fled from the delights of the world and its fame, honor ran after her, so all the people of Bethulia felt her piety, and everyone esteemed her and honored her.

And you, what have you given up of material things and lust for the sake of God? How great is your effort to be alone with God and to enjoy prayers and meditations? And how many souls have been influenced by you and drawn by you to the love of Christ?
(2) The rebuke of the elders of the city (vv. 9-13:)

9- Now when she heard that Ozias had promised to surrender the city after five days, she sent to the two elders Chabris and Karmi. 10- And they came to her, and she said to them, What is this thing which Ozias has agreed to, to surrender the city to the Assyrians if no help comes to us within five days? 11- Who are you that tempt the Lord? 12- This is not a word that obtains mercy, but rather stirs up wrath and kindles anger. 13- For you have set a term for the mercy of the Lord, and appointed him a day as it pleases you.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: She sent: she dispatched.

Judith sent to the chief elders of the city, the two elders Chabris and Karmi, who were perhaps the assistants of Ozias the head, or elder, of the city. She sent to them because she did not want to leave her solitude and walk in the streets of the city, and she did not summon Ozias the head of the city, either out of respect and regard for his position, or because she did not want to hinder him from leading the multitudes of the agitated and grieving people, so she called his assistants only.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: They came: they arrived at her house.

The two elders responded to Judith's call, because of her great spiritual standing in the city. When the two elders came, she rebuked them with all boldness and gentleness for what Ozias had declared and the elders had agreed to, since they yielded to the pressure of the people, when Ozias asked them to give God a respite of five days, and if He did not rescue them, they would surrender the city to the Assyrians.

And this opinion, although it was better than the opinion of the people, who wanted to surrender the city at once, was nevertheless a great error in the eyes of Judith, who, it seems, had a spiritual stature higher than all the rest.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Kindles: sets alight.
Indignation: severe anger.
A term: a period or the end of an appointed time.
Judith made clear the error of what Ozias had declared in two matters:

1- This is weakness of faith and doubt in God, indeed a tempting of Him, for Ozias gives God a respite to complete His work at an appointed time, otherwise he will surrender the city to the Assyrians, and this is not fitting at all.
For God is able to do all things and He should be waited for without limit, for we have none other than Him.

2- It is not proper, or humble, to place conditions on God that He may rescue us, but seeking His mercy is by submitting to Him and delivering our life completely, and He rescues us at the time He Himself sees, for He loves us and knows our good better than we do. She warned them that fixing a respite for God to work in provokes His wrath against them, because fixing a period means tempting God, and this greatly grieves God, as in (Ex 17:2-7, Mt 4:7). There is a difference between persistence and fixing a period for the work of God, because persistence and asking for God's quick intervention means faith, clinging to God, and waiting for His intervention with constant importunity toward Him. This is, of course, not the same as fixing a period, and if God does not act within it, leaving Him and looking for other solutions.

I wish that you would rely on God with complete faith and be confident that He does not forget you, even if afflictions increase upon you and despair fights you. Be strong and continue your prayers, to overcome evil thoughts, and you will always enjoy the mercies of God. (3) Their call to repentance (vv. 14-29:)
14- But since the Lord is long-suffering, let us repent of this and seek His forgiveness with tears poured out.

15- For the threat of God is not like the threat of man, neither does He burn with anger like the son of man. 16- Therefore let us humble our souls before Him and serve Him in a humble spirit. 17- And let us ask the Lord with tears to grant us His mercy according to His will, that we may glory in our humility, just as our hearts were troubled by their pride. 18- For we have not walked in the sins of our fathers, who left their God and worshiped strange gods. 19- For which iniquity they were delivered to the sword and to spoil and to shame among their enemies, but we know no other god than Him. 20- So let us hope in humility for His comfort, and He will avenge our blood on the oppression of our enemies against us, and will bring down all the nations that rise up against us, and the Lord our God will put them to shame. 21- And now, O brethren, since you are elders in the people of God and their souls depend on you, raise up their hearts by your words, that they may remember that it was only to prove our fathers whether they would truly worship their God that trial came upon them. 22- They should therefore remember how our father Abraham was tried, and after being proved by many tribulations became the friend of God. 23- And so Isaac, and so Jacob, and so Moses, and all those with whom God was pleased passed through many tribulations and remained faithful. 24- But those who did not receive the trials with the fear of the Lord, but showed their impatience, and their murmuring against the Lord returned upon them, 25- were destroyed by the destroyer and perished by serpents.

26- But as for us now, let us not be impatient at what we suffer. 27- But let us esteem these punishments to be less than our sins, and believe that the scourges of the Lord, with which we are chastened like servants, are for amendment and not for destruction. 28- Then Ozias and the elders said to her, All that you have said is true, and there is no fault in your words. 29- Now therefore pray for us, for you are a holy woman and fear God.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Burns: is kindled and his anger intensifies.
With anger: with rage and severe wrath.

Judith reassured the two elders that God is not like men, impetuous in His wrath or vengeance, and that He will not hasten to chastise the people for what they had resolved to do, so there is still an opportunity for repentance. She advised them to humble themselves before God with humility, tears, prayers and contrite worship together with the people, and God would forgive them for what they had said, and have mercy on them, and rescue them from the Assyrians as He sees fit and at the time He appoints, for His will is good, so they would triumph by this over their enemies and glory in this humility that brought upon them the mercies of God, instead of the turmoil that shook their hearts because of the pride and might of their enemies.
Humility is your way to win all the battles against the devil and to enjoy the fullness of the work of the divine power in you.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: We have walked: we have followed.

What reassures and encourages us is that we have not left our God and worshiped strange gods, but worship God alone; for when our fathers became proud and worshiped strange gods, God left them, and they were exposed to the aggression of the enemies around them with killing and plunder, so they fell into great shame, as happened in the days of the Judges and the wicked kings, when their neighbors attacked them and humbled them.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Oppression: that is, harshness, which means injustice and tyranny.
Those who rise up against us: those who leap upon us, that is, those who attack us.

By our faith in God and our humility before Him we ask for His mercies, and He rescues us from our enemies who wrong us, and puts them to shame, humbles them and takes vengeance on them, and so saves our souls.
Let us stand firm in the faith, and draw near to God in humility, hoping in Him at all times, and He will remove evils from us.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Depend: under your responsibility.
Raise up: encourage.

Judith continued her speech with the two elders. It seems that the news of her summoning the two elders had reached the head of the city, Ozias, and out of his regard for this great lady Judith, he felt the importance of the matter, and hurried in humility himself to her house to learn what she wanted in this severe trial through which their city Bethulia was passing. Perhaps he took it as an opportunity to receive a blessing from this pious woman, and he joined the two elders to listen to the guidance and teachings of this saint who by her piety and wisdom led her people in the way of God and brought about victory for it.

She said to them that since they were responsible for the souls of this people, they must alert them to an important spiritual principle, which is that God permits afflictions to test His children, and if they obey Him and hold fast to Him, they are proved and receive a great blessing.

It is to be noted that Judith did not speak to the people directly, out of her regard for the position and function of the elders responsible for teaching the people, who signify the role of the priests and deacons in the New Testament. It is not fitting for a woman to teach the people, except for teaching women and children.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: And she gave them examples, such as our father Abraham, whom God tested by his leaving his city and going out into the wilderness (Gen 32:1) and his offering Isaac his son as a sacrifice (Gen 22), so his faith was proved and he became the father of all the Jewish people, and God's promises were fulfilled in him. Also the holy fathers Isaac (Gen 22, 25:21) and Jacob (Gen 29-31) and Moses (Gen 34:1-4) and all who pleased the Lord and endured afflictions steadfast in their faith.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: The destroyer destroyed them: God exterminated them.

As for those who refused faith by murmuring, such as the people of Israel, who murmured in the wilderness of Sinai, after their going out from the land of Egypt, several times: for example, when they murmured against the manna, their heavenly food, and craved the meat and the onions and the leeks which were in the land of Egypt; or when they murmured at the scarcity of water; or when they were afraid to enter the promised land because of the inhabitants of the land, so they were prevented from entering it and those who were afraid died in the wilderness; and when they murmured against the manna and the quail, the serpents bit them.
So affliction is a blessing that God permits, so let us not murmur at it, lest we lose its blessings and God forsake us and we be exposed to greater afflictions and God be angry with us.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Be impatient: be afraid.
Less than our sins: less than our sins deserve.
Then Judith summarized how the people of Bethulia should conduct themselves in the face of this great affliction, as follows:
1- Not to be troubled by the difficulty of the affliction, but to stand firm in the faith and be reassured of God's care and His protection of us.

2- To look at our sins, that is, to examine ourselves and repent, and then we feel that we deserve afflictions far greater than this affliction because of the multitude of our sins; that is, the affliction leads us to deep repentance.

3- To be confident, despite the difficulty of the affliction, which shows our weakness as weak servants and not great masters, that it turns to our good and mends many of our faults and brings us near to God.

I wish that you would meditate on the blessings of the afflictions that have passed through your life and thank God for them, so that this is a safeguard for you against any turmoil that attacks you if a new affliction comes upon you.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: How great was the humility of Ozias, and of the elders Chabris and Karmi, before Judith. And how strong is the awe and influence of the words of the saints on those who listen to them. They felt their error in what they had declared to the people, and agreed with Judith in what she guided them to in her beautiful spiritual sermon.
They also felt that they were before a great saint, so they asked her to pray for them and for all the people.

In proportion to how much you live with God in holy worship and enjoy fellowship with Him in prayers and meditations, to that extent will be your spiritual influence on those around you, and your service will be successful, and you will win many souls.
(4) Her secret mission (vv. 30-34:)

30- Then Judith said to them, As you have known that what I have spoken is from God, 31- so know about what I have resolved that it is from God, and pray that God may confirm my counsel. 32- This night you shall stand at the gate, and I will go out with my maidservant, and pray that the Lord may look upon His people Israel in the five days as you have said. 33- And I do not wish that you inquire into my purpose, and from now until I tell you of it, do nothing but pray to the Lord our God for us. 34- Then Ozias said to her, Judah commands you, go in peace, and may the Lord be with you in taking vengeance on our enemies. And they departed, returning

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Judith ended her speech with the elders, that since they had trusted in her faith and her teaching, which they had agreed to, she asked them to trust in what she would do, for with her experience and fellowship with God she was confident that her conduct was sound, and she asked for their prayers that God would complete His work with her for the rescue of His people.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: Then Judith asked the elders to stand at the gate of the city that night, to bid her farewell and bless her as she went out with her maidservant to meet the enemies, and she repeated her request that they pray for her, that God might rescue His people during the coming five days.

Despite her refusal to fix a period for the work of God, she was confident that God in His love would condescend and rescue them before the expiry of this respite, out of compassion for His people, making allowance for them in the weakness of their faith.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: And she asked two things of them:
1- Not to ask about the nature of her mission and its details.
2- To pray for her, that God might complete the rescue of His people by her hands.

Judith bore alone the responsibility of rescuing her people, and told no one the details of her mission, because she had compassion on those around her, lest their faith in God's help for her be shaken, in addition to the fact that their compassion for her might lead them to prevent her from carrying out her mission.
When you find those around you in weakness, instead of blaming them for their weakness, bear the responsibility in their place, and help them and rescue them by the power of God from their troubles.

entries.section: (3) The thirst of the people and their demand to surrender the city

paragraphs.text: When the elders heard this surprise, that is, Judith's secret mission, they submitted to her words, and Ozias, the head of the city, spoke in their name. The Holy Bible calls him here "the prince of Judah," considering that the temple of God in Jerusalem belongs to the tribe of Judah, and the city of Bethulia believes in the God who dwells in the temple in Jerusalem, so their head is called prince of Judah... And he told her to go in the peace of God to complete her mission, raising prayers for her, that God might help her and rescue His people by her hands.

The three elders departed from her house, and perhaps they went to the synagogue, or to one of the houses, and gathered to pray for Judith, then went to wait for her at the gate of the city, and stood there in prayer waiting for her to go out that night, as she had told them, to complete her mission. Their feelings were all reverence and awe, because of the difficulty of her mission and compassion for her because of the difficulty of the situation, and at the same time confidence in her holiness and the power of God supporting her was stirring in their hearts, while the sense of the people's humiliation through thirst and their nearness to death tormented them, as they besought God for His quick answer and His compassion on them. It was the sense of responsibility together with the sense of weakness before the difficulty of the situation; so they humbled themselves before God, waiting for His salvation.
The prayer of Judith before she left the city

entries.section: (1) Remembering God's works in rescuing His people

paragraphs.text: Her shrine: her upper room in which she worships.

After the elders left the house of Judith, she went up to her upper room where she lived, and where she was accustomed to offer many prayers, so as to cast herself before God in humility. She put on sackcloth more than she usually wore, in reverence and humility, that God might have mercy on her, and she even put ashes on her head. That is, she smeared her head and her hair, which was her crown, with the dust of the earth, in contrition before the Lord. This was in the evening, at the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice in Jerusalem, as the translation of the Jesuit Fathers tells us, so that her prayers might rise with the smoke ascending from the sacrifice to heaven. That sacrifice points to Christ the Redeemer, in whom all prayers are accepted.
She bowed down before the Lord in submission, opened her heart, and cried out to Him from the depths with a fervent prayer, because she had no refuge or helper except Him.
This confirms Judith's complete reliance on God and not on her own gifts, and her trust and faith in His power, which is able to do all things.

May we, in trials and afflictions, learn from Judith to cast ourselves before God, so that we find our complete strength, laying at His feet all the abilities that He has given us, should He wish to use them.

entries.section: (1) Remembering God's works in rescuing His people

paragraphs.text: At the beginning of her prayer she made her supplication to God, the God of her fathers, who is distinguished by His power above every human strength, who gave her father Simeon son of Jacob strength in the incident of the violation of his sister Dinah by Shechem son of Hamor (Gen 34). Simeon killed the adulterer, his father, and all the men of the city. This was a punishment that God permitted for this adulterer and his clan, although Simeon and his brother Levi were driven by their anger, and their father Jacob rebuked them severely. But here Judith focuses on the power of God who takes vengeance on sinners, who defiled His virgin Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and who now want to defile His virgin, that is, His city Bethulia, and indeed all the cities of Israel, by killing, plundering and destroying them.

Thus God turned the evil back upon the one who did it, that is, upon the city of Shechem. As they had violated Dinah, their wives and daughters became captives of the sons of Jacob, and likewise all their possessions. Judith humbly asked Him to help her, a weak widow, against the mighty enemies, because He is the God who is able to work through the weakest of the weak.

By your humility you can draw out the mercies of God and overcome all the powers of the world. The evil of the wicked then turns upon their own heads, and you escape easily, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.

entries.section: (1) Remembering God's works in rescuing His people

paragraphs.text: All Your ways are prepared; all Your plans are made ready.

Then she attributes the ordering of the universe to God. He is its Creator and Governor from its beginning and the Ruler of all, able by His wisdom to order matters so that they lead to the good of His children, that He may complete His care for them. He is the Eternal, the Everlasting, the Creator and Governor of all creatures, and therefore they are subject to the plans of God, who permitted the attack of the Assyrians and their siege of her city, but at the same time God turns all this to their good.
It is a wonderful reassurance that the children of God enjoy, because of their trust that God is the Ruler of all, and that all His ways are upright and their aim is the care of His children.

entries.section: (1) Remembering God's works in rescuing His people

paragraphs.text: You troubled them: You disturbed them.
Clung: stuck.

Judith reminded God of His support of His people, whom Moses led in ancient times as they fled from Egypt and came to the Red Sea, when Pharaoh, the greatest king in the world at that time, went out after them with his mighty army, his chariots and his horsemen. She recalled how God looked down upon them in His power, by the pillar of fire that separated between them and His people and troubled their horses and horsemen, and because of the intensity of the face of the fire they saw nothing, as though it were darkness. Then He parted the Red Sea, and the children of Israel crossed on dry land to the other shore. As for the Egyptians, when they entered into the midst of the sea, their feet stuck to its bottom and the water covered them, so that they were in deep darkness and all of them died.

entries.section: (2) Asking for victory over the enemies

paragraphs.text: Judith asked that God treat the Assyrians as He treated the Egyptians of old and destroy them, however great their power and however proud they were of their strength and weapons.

entries.section: (2) Asking for victory over the enemies

paragraphs.text: Destroys: crushes and wipes out.

What was hidden from our enemies is their not knowing You, the great God, besides whom there is none other, and that You are our own God who defends us, and that You are the Master and Lord of all the earth. How else did they dare to fight us, except that they do not know You and are ignorant of Your power? It is You who crush the power of enemies in wars and triumph over them, however great their strength.

entries.section: (2) Asking for victory over the enemies

paragraphs.text: And now the time has come, our God, for You to lift Your hand and shatter the power of the enemies who intend to attack Your people and Your city Jerusalem and Your temple and Your great altar, where You dwell. It is well known that the children of Israel held fast to the temple of God and revered it, and were ready to defend it even to death, so that it deeply troubled them that any harm should befall it.

entries.section: (3) Asking for strength to kill Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Judith moves from speaking about the enemy in general, that is, the Assyrian army, to speaking about the head of this army, Holofernes, who represents it and leads it. She asks God to shatter his pride and cut him off from the earth, for how can a man be proud against God, who protects His people? To humiliate him still further, she asked that God kill him with his own weapon and not with the weapons of the children of Israel, to show him his weakness before the power of God.

entries.section: (3) Asking for strength to kill Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Be caught: be hunted and fall like prey in a net.
In her prayer to God Judith began to reveal her secret plan, which was to trap Holofernes himself, the greatest head of the army, for then she would be able to defeat the whole army.

In this she made use of the evil that was in Holofernes, as a Gentile man whose gods were his lusts. She was a very beautiful woman, and because he was wicked, he would be caught by his evil gaze at her bodily beauty, and he would be changed from a great commander into a humble slave beneath her feet. Likewise her gentle words would rob him of his will and strip him of all his strength. Some may ask about Judith's method of deceiving and attracting Holofernes by her beauty, and say that this does not agree with her holiness and chastity. We answer that deception is permitted in war, as God Himself declared in the story of the victory over Ai in the days of Joshua, by setting an ambush (Josh 8:1-9). Judith would hold fast to her purity, but Holofernes in his lust could not bear Judith's beauty. Holofernes and the Assyrian chiefs were known for indulgence in sexual lusts, as is mentioned in (ch. 12:11).
May we be watchful lest we fall through our weakness. The devil has no authority over us, but we are caught in his nets if lust controls us.
Are we drawn by beautiful sights and soft words, or by God who is hidden behind all earthly beauty? Are we seeking God or lust?

entries.section: (3) Asking for strength to kill Holofernes

paragraphs.text: At the same time Judith felt her weakness, so she asked God to protect her as a weak woman, lest her heart be affected by his power and greatness. As long as a person is strong within, through God who dwells in him, he stands firm before all temptations and difficult circumstances that he must pass through in his life. She even asked God for strength to despise evil, that is, for the greatness and glory of this commander to become rejected and hateful in her eyes, and then she asks for further help so that she might be able to destroy him.

If you feel the harms of sin, you will hate it, and the lust that delights human eyes will become despised by you. Then you will be able easily, by the power of the Holy Spirit dwelling in you, to overcome all the power of the enemy, Satan.

entries.section: (3) Asking for strength to kill Holofernes

paragraphs.text: And when God is glorified through a weak widow, and a widow is one who has no husband, if a person feels spiritually that he is this widow, God will be the husband of this widow, that is, her strength. He will crush all the powers of evil before him, and then all the glory will be God's and not the weak human being's.
Present your weakness before God as a needy widow, and God will be glorified with all His power in you.

entries.section: (4) God's power is for the humble

paragraphs.text: Then Judith concludes her profound prayer by affirming that God's power is for the weak who take refuge in Him, who feel their weakness before Him and their dependence on Him, and not on their weapons, their strength and their numbers.

entries.section: (4) God's power is for the humble

paragraphs.text: As she affirmed this truth, she felt the greatness of God, exalted in heaven, the Creator of all things and the Creator of the waters from which He brought forth all that exists. And since He is the Creator of the waters, He is able to quench the thirst of His children in Bethulia by sending down abundant rain from heaven for many days. For the weapon of the enemies with which they fight the people of God, namely water, is also in the hand of God, the Ruler of all. At the same time she felt her weakness and lowliness before His greatness, so she asked that her prayer be answered and that He encompass her with His mercies.

entries.section: (4) God's power is for the humble

paragraphs.text: In my mouth: in my mouth.

She reminded Him of His promises to the fathers, that is, the care of His people, through the intercession of the holy Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and likewise Moses and all the prophets, that He might give her wisdom in speech, and even put His irresistible word in her mouth, establish in her heart what she had resolved, and support her, so that she might defeat the commander of the Assyrian armies. For when God defeats the Assyrians, He declares clearly to all the world that He alone is God above all the gods of the nations, who were defeated by the Assyrians.
From this last verse appears Judith's longing to proclaim the name of God to all the nations. She wants everyone to believe in God and to live under His care.

Is your aim the glorification of God when you ask for His help, or the glorification of yourself? May you hide yourself, so that God appears and works in you freely, defeats all the evils within you, and lifts you above all, and you become, without feeling it, a light to the nations and salt of the earth.
Judith goes out of the city to meet Holofernes

entries.section: (1) Judith prepares for her secret mission

paragraphs.text: Judith began her prayer in the evening and continued for many hours, until it was near midnight, in fervent prayers, humbled before God, part of which the previous chapter has recorded for us. After she finished her prayer, she rose from her prostration and came down from her upper room, in which she worships God.

entries.section: (1) Judith prepares for her secret mission

paragraphs.text: Her widowhood: her being a widow.

Judith went down to her house and summoned her own maidservant to help her in her great mission. She took off the coarse garments that she wore as asceticism, self-denial and humility before God, and she also took off the clothes that she used to wear during her widowhood after the death of her husband, that is, the simple, plain clothes, like the clothes of nuns, or of consecrated women today.

entries.section: (1) Judith prepares for her secret mission

paragraphs.text: Bracelets: ornaments worn around the wrist, usually of gold.
Earrings: what is worn in the ear and used to adorn it.
Lilies: plural of lily, a beautiful flower of various colors, some kinds of which have a sweet fragrance, and which is widespread in the Mediterranean basin.

Then she began to care for her body. She bathed and anointed her body with perfumes and fragrant oils and all the materials with which a woman beautifies her appearance and her body, until she became very beautiful and attractive in appearance.

She arranged her hair (it seems that the fine style at that time was for a woman to part her hair), and her hair flowed down in a beautiful manner. She put on her loveliest garments, joyful in their colors and beautiful in form, then put a tiara on her head to increase her radiance and beauty, and put beautiful sandals on her feet. She chose the finest of the jewelry she had, adorning her arms with golden bracelets, and her ears with earrings, and her garments with ornaments in the form of beautiful lilies, and she put rings on her fingers. She used all the means of adornment she had, and she became very beautiful.

entries.section: (1) Judith prepares for her secret mission

paragraphs.text: Through her many prayers over the years she had gained a strong relationship with God and an ability to hear His voice. So when she lifted up her prayers for the affliction of her people, God guided her to this strange way, namely using her beauty to defend herself and her people while keeping her modesty and purity. Self-defense is a difficult situation, in which it is permitted to kill the attacker, or to draw him away from destroying a life by beauty or by any other means, while keeping personal purity in body and thought. This means that it is not right to use beauty as a means of enticement to reach personal ends in dealing with others. But Judith's case is a special case, because she and her people were exposed to death. It was a case of self-defense, and she undertook nothing of this until after a long prayer in which she cast herself before God. Judith appeared in wonderful beauty, which dazzled her maidservant, because God, who guided her to this means, granted her to appear very beautiful, more than any woman in her beauty adorned with such adornment, for she adorned herself out of virtue, namely her readiness to lay down her life for God and to defend her people, and her heart was in complete purity, with no evil lust in it.

entries.section: (1) Judith prepares for her secret mission

paragraphs.text: Wineskin: a vessel of leather in which wine was kept.

She prepared what she needed on her journey of food and drink, so that she might remain faithful to God's law in her food and not eat the food of the Gentiles, since the Jewish law forbade certain foods. So she prepared foods and gave them to her maidservant, the most important of them being bread, cheese and dried figs, and also wine, which is fermented grape juice, customarily drunk as a popular drink in the land of Judea, where vineyards abound, and which is different from the wine known today with its high alcohol content. In addition she also took oil and flour to make food, in case the bread and the food she had should run out. The translation of the Jesuit Fathers of this book mentions that the bread was of barley, which is the lowest kind of bread, and this shows her adherence to asceticism.

These preparations took a few hours of the night, and when she finished her preparation it was the time before dawn, about an hour before daybreak. So she went out of her house in this pitch darkness, with a courageous heart, relying on her God, to accomplish His will and to defend her people.

God has granted you many gifts and abilities. Do you use them in your spiritual striving against the devil? Do you spend all your energy in your spiritual wars against sin? May your only aim be God and the fulfilment of His will, and the rejection of your personal aims, especially evil aims, and every evil lust. Then you will act with a good conscience in all your conduct, and seek only to please God. Be sure that God will then bless you and support you, make all your ways prosper, and make all subject to you, that is, give you reverence in the eyes of all.

Hold fast to the commandments of God in all your ways, however difficult your circumstances, and do not make the excuse that it is impossible to carry out the commandment. Hold fast to the small commandments as to the great ones, and so you show the purity of your heart and your submission to God, and you will receive all His help in your life.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: Judith and her maidservant walked from her house toward the gate of the city, in the darkness and stillness of the night. When the two reached the gate of the city, they found Uzziah and the elders of the city waiting for her, their hearts lifted up to God in prayer for Judith and for the people.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: The surprise was in the change of her appearance, her clothes, her shining adornment and her captivating beauty. They were greatly amazed, because they did not know the nature of her secret mission, and because they had not seen her for years in such an attractive appearance.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: The elders kept what they had promised her, that is, not to ask about her secret mission, and Uzziah raised a prayer of blessing and supplication in the name of the elders of the city, that God might grant her strong help and support, so that God's salvation of His people might be accomplished at her hands, and all Jerusalem and the whole Jewish nation might be proud of her. Thus her holiness appears, and her name is joined to the names of the holy children of God.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: After Uzziah's prayer all who stood there, the elders of the city and the gatekeepers, said Amen, sharing in raising prayers and supplication for her. Then the elders of the city ordered the gatekeepers to open the gate, since it was kept closed night and day because of the siege of the Assyrians, and they opened it at dawn.

How great is prayer, for it gives a person favor in the eyes of all, so that they trust him and obey him, and all the closed doors are opened to him. May we trust in prayer and its effect on those around us, however strange our words may seem to our hearers. The word of God may not be acceptable to the people of the world, but through prayer they submit to it, and so we can accomplish our secret mission, which is the salvation of our souls and the souls of others, and pass through all the closed doors, leaving the world behind us, to reach the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: Daybreak: the beginning of the day, that is, dawn.
Judith and her maidservant went out and came down from the mountain, on which their city was built, at the beginning of the rising of dawn.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: She was praying, asking for God's help in great humility, and at the foot of the mountain the advance guards of the Assyrian soldiers surrounding the city saw her. They hurried to the two women and asked them where they had come from and where they were going.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: Hebrews: named after Abraham, who crossed over from between the two rivers to the land of Canaan, and after Eber, one of Abraham's forefathers. The people of God were famous by this name at the beginning of their history, but afterward they were called the children of Israel, and then the Jews.
Was convinced: became sure.
Despised: treated as of little account.
Refused: declined.
Willingly: by their own will.

Judith answered that she was a Hebrew from Bethulia, and that she was convinced of the weakness of the city before the power of the Assyrian armies and admitted the mistake of her people when they refused to surrender their city and ask the mercy of the Assyrians, and for this reason they would fall as prey to their vengeance.

This is certainly according to ordinary human thinking, not according to faith. So she did not lie, as it seems at first glance, but spoke of a logical, clear and certain reality. But faith is above reality, and even affirms its opposite at times. This is what Judith hid in her heart and did not declare.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: Because of this logical fact, namely the weakness of the city of Bethulia before the mighty army of the Assyrians, Judith fled from among them to escape destruction and to become a guide for Holofernes in his war against her city, so that he would not kill anyone of his army.

And indeed Judith fled from her city to save herself from death, and even to save all her people. She became a guide for Holofernes in storming the city, and he did storm it, but as a dead man at the hand of Judith, and his head reached the city, not to see what was inside it, for his eyes could no longer see, but to be hung upon the wall of the city. And none of his soldiers was lost, for all his mighty army fled in terror, leaving behind what they owned, after their commander was killed at the hand of Judith.

In any case, even if some think that these words of hers contain deception and disguise, she was in a state of war, that is, of self-defense, and in this situation the laws of war permit deception. This is like what happened when God commanded His people Israel to maneuver against the men of Ai: one company attacked and then retreated as though defeated, and drew the army of Ai out of the city after it, and another company that was hidden behind the city attacked it and destroyed it (Josh 8).

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: Then the grace of God appears to Judith, for the soldiers of Holofernes were dazzled by her beauty and sympathized with her, and no doubt crossed their minds about her words. For it was customary, when enemies besieged cities, for some of their inhabitants to flee, and the besiegers would seize them and use them as spies, so that it would be easy to take their cities.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes' soldiers seize Judith

paragraphs.text: Saved: from preservation, which is protection.
You will stand in the best place in his heart: he will welcome you, be pleased with you and admire you.

The soldiers praised Judith's action, because by fleeing from her city she had saved herself from death, and they assured her that their commander would treat her well when he saw her. Then they took her to his tent. Perhaps these words reassured Judith of the success of her mission, because the Gentiles are sensual, and for them the aim of war is to gain captives and spoils and it is not a holy war, as it is with the children of God. Judith had adorned herself, but without any lust, wanting only the glory of God and the rescue of her country. And because of the evil of the pagans and the faith of the children of God in Him, He intervenes, gives victory to His children and defeats the wicked.

When a person puts the fear of God in his heart and strives to fulfil His will, God gives him favor in the eyes of all and makes his ways easy. Let us then set in our souls to please God, hold fast to His commandments, worship Him faithfully and serve Him with all our energies, and trust that God will bless and complete His work in us and make us prosper in everything, as long as we have no purpose besides Him.

entries.section: (3) Her entry to Holofernes

paragraphs.text: The Assyrian soldiers led Judith to the tent of their commander Holofernes, and the chiefs and officers of the army gathered in crowds to see the beauty of this woman and to inquire about the reason for her presence at this early hour of the morning before the commander's tent.
Judith was the first woman of the Jewish race to appear before the Assyrians, and they admired her greatly, and consequently all the women of the Hebrews.

The guards sleeping at the entrance of Holofernes' tent woke up and came out to find out what was happening, and when they saw Judith and were dazzled by her, they went in and told their commander, who was lying on his bed.

entries.section: (3) Her entry to Holofernes

paragraphs.text: His attendants: the police under him, of officers and soldiers.
Worthy: deserving.
Despises: holds in contempt.

Likewise all the officers of Holofernes and his guards who accompanied him, who in their great admiration for the beauty of Judith praised the people of Israel, who have women of such beauty. They even advised Holofernes that if the women of the Hebrews were so beautiful, they were spoil worth fighting to win, confirming by this how deeply they were moved and how they had submitted under the sway of Judith's beauty, by the grace of God which He had given her.

entries.section: (3) Her entry to Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Purple: cloth of a dark red color.
Emerald: a precious stone of green color.

Judith looked at the spacious tent of Holofernes and saw that it was divided into parts like rooms, and adorned with shining red purple fabrics, gold, and precious stones, of emerald and various jewels. Holofernes had risen from his bedchamber to the reception room and sat on a great seat, and they brought Judith in to him.

entries.section: (3) Her entry to Holofernes

paragraphs.text: As for Judith, she stood silent, which added to her beauty, then bowed down to the ground in submission and gentle lowliness, and remained prostrate with the eyes of all fixed upon her, until Holofernes ordered his soldiers to raise her up. She stood in his presence with her beauty shining before all. Thus she showed her submission to him, and drew his heart still more to her.

Judith bowed down before the commander Holofernes in weakness and humility, while in truth Holofernes and his soldiers had already submitted under her feet and been caught by her beauty. She is the strong one, despite the appearance of weakness upon her. She is the Church, which appears subject to the authority of the world and its rulers, yet she is the one who influences the whole world through her Christ who dwells in her. She is a light to the whole world. So it is with all the holy children of God, just as Paul stood in chains before Felix the governor and spoke words of grace, and the governor, sitting on his throne, trembled at the power of his words (Acts 24:25).
If you trust in God who dwells in you, then despite your silence and your apparent weakness, God gives you beauty and reverence, and all respect you and submit to your word.
How much every father and mother and every servant needs faith in God who dwells in him, so that he can draw hearts with power and ease.
Judith's meeting with Holofernes

entries.section: (1) Holofernes welcomes Judith

paragraphs.text: Be of good cheer: let your soul be at rest.
Fear: dread.
Preferred: chose rather.

The first meeting between Holofernes and Judith began, with his officers standing before him in his great tent, and he sitting on his throne. He began his conversation with Judith by reassuring her, so that she would not be disturbed by the splendor of the place, its might, and the might of his soldiers, and he asked her to calm her mind and be of good heart.

Holofernes was clearly moved by Judith's beauty and gentleness, for God had given her grace, not only in attractive beauty, but so that whoever sees her feels comfort and reassurance and is at ease with her. For this reason Holofernes was kind and gentle with her.

In reassuring Judith, Holofernes tried to give her an impression of himself and to suggest to her that he was peaceable and not inclined to harm, and that he never harmed any peaceful person who was subject to King Nebuchadnezzar. This is completely contrary to the truth, as we learned from the previous chapters, for the nations who submitted to him, he destroyed their cities and burned them and killed many of them. But he tries to win Judith's affection and to depart from his savage nature.

entries.section: (1) Holofernes welcomes Judith

paragraphs.text: I would have raised my spear: I would have lifted my spear, meaning that I had decided to discipline them.

In Holofernes' speech about Judith's people, he spoke courteously, declaring that he had not intended to harm them, and that he had been compelled to besiege the city and prepare to fight it with his soldiers and weapons because they were the ones who had committed an unforgivable error, in that they had despised him by not surrendering themselves and their city to him.

The power of influence of the meek children of God upon the people of the wicked world turns them to meekness and calms their savage nature. When lambs are sent out in the midst of wolves, as the Lord Christ said to His disciples (Lk 10:3), they can change the nature of the savage wolves into the nature of the gentle lamb, for the lambs are stronger than the wolves, since the power of God is in them.

May you not meet the anger of others with greater anger, nor their pride with harsher pride, but by your humility and meekness break every anger and pride, as the Holy Bible says: "A soft answer turneth away wrath" (Prov 15:1).

entries.section: (1) Holofernes welcomes Judith

paragraphs.text: After Holofernes had reassured Judith and declared his love, forbearance and esteem for her, he asked her to explain to him why she had left her city, come to him, and preferred to take refuge with the Assyrians. Although the reason for her coming had reached him through the advance guards of his soldiers, who had seized her as she came down from the mountain, he wanted to verify it himself and, as the one in charge, learn the facts from her in detail.

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: Judith began her long conversation with Holofernes in humility, declaring that she was his maidservant and slave and asking his permission for him to listen to her. She even drew his heart to her, not by beauty alone, but by wisdom, for she promised him victory and the achievement of his aims if he would listen to her words.

The beautiful thing is that she did not leave her faith and creed out of her speech, but declared that this was from the Lord, to the point that at the end of the conversation (v. 21) Holofernes declared his readiness to submit to her great God. So she was like a missionary to him and to his soldiers, that perhaps they might believe. In her wisdom and humility she resembles Abigail in her conversation with David (1 Sam 25).

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: The wayward souls: the souls that are full of evil and rebel and go astray, and do not submit to Holofernes.
The wild beasts of the field: all the beasts that live on the earth.
Be led by him: submit to him.

After Judith had drawn Holofernes with the hope of achieving his aims, she praised him and his lord King Nebuchadnezzar. She wished him life, which is what every great man desires, to remain in his greatness, and she declared his authority over the whole earth, because he had taken many of the cities of the world around him. For her hearers this meant the hope of taking all the kingdoms of the earth. She glorified the power of the king, which appears in Holofernes, and in this way she turned the praise toward Holofernes, and even regarded him as the true power that ought to be praised, for without him the lord Nebuchadnezzar is worth nothing.

She also praised the authority of Holofernes and Nebuchadnezzar in subjecting everyone who opposes them, or whose heart tempts him to resist them, and by this all people, and even animals and beasts, submit to them.

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: Judith also commended his intelligence and wisdom in managing such a mighty army and the kingdoms he had taken. Indeed, everyone agrees that Holofernes alone is distinguished by a mighty power which no one rivals with King Nebuchadnezzar, especially after Holofernes took many lands and subdued them. He is capable in his management and in his military strength, which subdues the nations to him. These words are true and not flattery on Judith's part, because he really is intelligent, strong and a shrewd politician.

Every person is affected by praise, and a good word gladdens hearts. So if you want to win the heart of any person, however harsh he may be or far from you, offer him a word of praise or encouragement. May you see the virtues of others and praise them for these, so that you encourage them and win them, and at the same time benefit from these virtues, to acquire them and grow in your spiritual life.

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: After she opened her speech with praise, and Holofernes' heart was ready to believe and accept all that she said, she told him that she knew his decisions against Achior, and declared that she knew Achior's conversation with Holofernes, for Achior had related it to the people of Bethulia when he entered their city.

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: At the same time she confirmed what Achior had said, for she did not give up her faith in the crushing power of her God, but affirmed the truth that Achior had explained to them, that the mighty God of Israel is against them when they sin against Him, and consequently it would be easy for Holofernes to triumph over them. Judith confirmed her words with God's rebukes of His people through the mouth of His prophets for their sins, and His threat of destruction against them for their evils.

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: Then she described the state of her people as being in great terror since they heard the news of the army of Holofernes that besieges them, and she attributed this to their wrongdoing against their God. In this she does not lie, for the person who is strong in his faith and perfect in his trust in God is never disturbed. But this does not mean that God will destroy them, for God makes allowance for His children and helps their weak faith.

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: Had overtaken them: had increased upon them.
Lack of water: the need for water.

She pictured their suffering and distress, their severe hunger, and how thirst had increased upon them and they were near death. This is indeed true, but God is glorified in the weak, and the more the affliction increases, the nearer it comes to its solution.

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: To show the wrong of the people of God, Judith told how their thirst had increased so greatly that they were about to slaughter their cattle to drink their blood, which is contrary to the Law.

entries.section: (2) Judith informs Holofernes of her people's distress

paragraphs.text: Likewise the tithes and firstfruits that they consecrate to God, they were about to take because of the severity of thirst and hunger, although they had not yet done any of this. But Judith is trying to give logical grounds for God's anger against them, for they would break the Law and God would abandon them. Yet God is merciful and appreciates the distress of His children, so He is not angry with them, since they are in a state of death and not in contempt for God's holy things, nor with an intention to break the Law.

God is just and merciful, and Judith focused on the first attribute, but it does not stand without the second. In this she supported Holofernes, and at the same time she did not lie, but the mercy of God will appear, which helps His people and rescues them by the favor of His grace and not because they deserve it, since they are sinners. If Judith focused on one part of the truth, which is justice, and did not mention mercy, this is not permission for you always to state half-truths, for you may give a meaning opposite to the truth. We stress here that Judith was in very difficult circumstances, awaiting death and trying to defend herself and her people.

May you be, along with your justice, merciful in making allowances for others, especially if you are responsible for them, giving them a chance to correct their mistake and encouraging them, as God treats you with His mercy and love.

entries.section: (3) Judith is sent from God to Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Judith continues her speech in humility, describing herself as a slave, and says that she learned and understood all that had happened to the people of God, and God sent her to inform Holofernes of it.

This shows the extent of Judith's faith in what God had revealed to her and sent her on this dangerous mission. This revelation may have been by way of a vision or a dream, as appears in many places in the Holy Bible, such as the dreams of Joseph (Gen 37:5) and the visions and dreams of Paul (Acts 16:9; 18:9). By the power of her words she convinced Holofernes, and he believed that her God had sent her to him, so he was reassured and made her many promises, as appears in (vv. 20, 21). Thus the plan of God appears, which Judith carried out by several means, namely:
1- Her dazzling beauty.
2- Her praise of Holofernes.
3- Her submission to him.
4- Her convincing Holofernes that her people were in the wrong and deserved divine punishment.
5- Her speaking with confidence that she was sent by God to Holofernes to accompany him in his entry into Bethulia (and indeed she did enter, with his head with her).

entries.section: (3) Judith is sent from God to Holofernes

paragraphs.text: "Sheep that have no shepherd": an expression known in the Holy Bible meaning the absence of leadership and the weakness of the people, as in (Num 27:17, 1 Kgs 22:17, Mt 9:36). "Not a dog shall bark at you": an expression among the Semites, that is, the ancient tribes that lived in Asia, and it means calm and the absence of opposition and resistance from people, or even from animals such as the dog. Then she informed him of her intention that she would worship God in prayers and keep the Law, until God declares to her the proper time at which she would accompany Holofernes into the midst of Jerusalem.

Thus she persuaded Holofernes to let her practice her worship in his camp, because in that was his benefit, while in truth she wanted to pray and lean on the strong arm of God, that He might accomplish His salvation by her hands. Truly the people of Israel were in the wrong, and troubled like sheep that have no shepherd, and indeed no one could stand firm before Holofernes, but his end would be destruction. This is what Judith meant. But if anyone doubts whether Judith's inexact speech falls under the heading of plain lying and deception, let us make allowance for her, since her circumstances were difficult and she was in a state of self-defense, as she and her people faced the danger of death. We repeat that this is not permission for anyone to deceive in speech to the point of lying, except in war and military maneuvers, as Jael deceived Sisera (Judg 4:17-22) and as Joshua sent two spies to Jericho (Josh 2:1-7). Perhaps when Holofernes heard these words from Judith he thought she was a prophetess, or a priestess of her god, who could hear his voice and tell the future and divine guidance. This was known in pagan worship, and they greatly respected prophetesses and priestesses in the temples of the pagan gods.

How great it is for a person to hold fast to his spiritual life in the hardest places and the most adverse circumstances, and God will give him wisdom and opportunity to fulfil his acts of worship, and even make others agree with him and not hinder him.

entries.section: (3) Judith is sent from God to Holofernes

paragraphs.text: From Judith's words appears her deep relationship with God and her fervent prayers, to which she had been accustomed in her solitude for three and a half years. When this affliction swept over her city, God guided her to this means to save her people, so she is sent by Him to accomplish this work, which we believe God revealed to her clearly, although it is not stated openly in this book. But it is understood from this verse and the other verses in this chapter and before it and after it, because it is impossible for a person to know this strange plan to rescue his people. Despite this divine revelation to Judith, her carrying out of God's plan shows:
1- Her strong faith in the word of God.
2- Her indescribable courage in facing the cruelest personality in the world at that time.
3- Her severe asceticism and her holding fast to worship in all its details, of prayers and fasts.

4- Her readiness to die in obedience to God and to rescue her people. She is a type of Christ the Redeemer, for she entered into death, that is, the private chamber of Holofernes, and came out victorious with the head of Holofernes with her, as Christ died and Satan was bound.

entries.section: (3) Judith is sent from God to Holofernes

paragraphs.text: In conclusion Judith affirmed that God had become angry with His people because of their many sins, and consequently the way is open for Holofernes to fight them and take their city. She did not mention that God in His mercy forgives His people if they return to Him, and consequently Holofernes would become powerless before the power of God that protects them.

It is good that your life be a mission from God, to do His will, and that your only aim be the salvation of your soul and of others. So do not be disturbed if people think ill of you and do not understand you, as long as you are fulfilling the will of God with a pure heart.

entries.section: (4) Holofernes' praise and promises to Judith

paragraphs.text: When Holofernes and his soldiers standing around Judith heard these words and all her previous speech, they sensed the wisdom she possessed, which was no less than her enchanting beauty, and they praised the soundness of her mind and the goodness of her appearance, which they had never seen in another woman.

It is the grace of God that He pours out upon His children, so that the people of the world glorify them and submit to them, because the true power in a person is the power hidden within him, that is, the power of God who dwells in him, and not the power of outward appearances. This power is what makes everyone submit to him.

entries.section: (4) Holofernes' praise and promises to Judith

paragraphs.text: Then Holofernes spoke and praised the God of Israel, who guided Judith to hand Bethulia over to him, since Holofernes, like any person, thinks of his own interest. He admired the God of Israel because He achieves his interests and also the interest of Judith, who would be saved from destruction along with the rest of the city.

entries.section: (4) Holofernes' praise and promises to Judith

paragraphs.text: Will be spoken of: will be pointed out or her name mentioned.

He promised Judith that if she completed her mission and he took the city, he would take the God of Israel as his god, that is, as one of the gods he worships. He also promised her that she would have a special place in the palace of King Nebuchadnezzar and that he would testify for her and magnify what she had done, for the service of the Assyrians.

Do you worship God because He achieves your interests and demands? Or because you have been moved by His love and want to worship Him out of love for Him? Beware lest your heart be occupied with the material promises of the world, of wealth and greatness, for all these pass away. What truly matters is your standing before God and your eternal life.
Judith and Holofernes alone in his tent

entries.section: (1) Judith's prayers and fasts in the camp of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: After the first meeting between Judith and Holofernes, in which she won his great admiration for her beauty and his esteem for her wisdom, so that he agreed with her in all that she said and even declared his readiness to follow her God, because of the holiness he saw in her and her devotion to this God who would give him victory, Holofernes ordered that a dwelling be prepared for her in the best of places, far from the tents of the soldiers and officers, beside the storehouses of his treasures of gold, silver and precious stones. To honor her he also ordered that she be served the finest food and drink, from what was served to him personally.

entries.section: (1) Judith's prayers and fasts in the camp of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: But Judith, with all strength and trust in her God, refused to partake of his food and drink, because partaking of them was counted a sin according to the law of her God. Rather she resolved to eat what she had brought with her, of food prepared according to her law.

May you have faith and hold fast to the commandment, however embarrassing the surrounding circumstances. Do not be afraid to declare that worldly food, or speech, or dress does not suit you, but is counted as sin and a stumbling block before God, even though others do it. God must be obeyed rather than men, and be sure that God will give you favor in their eyes, so that they will not prevent you from carrying out the commandment.

entries.section: (1) Judith's prayers and fasts in the camp of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: As your soul lives: a phrase said not only as a prayer for life but as an oath, that is, "By your life, what I say must be accomplished." Of course the Law permitted oaths in the Old Testament.

Out of concern for Judith and love for her, Holofernes asked what she would do, and from where she would get food when what she had with her ran out. Judith replied with full confidence that it would not run out until God accomplished her mission and what she was thinking of. Before this confidence and strength and the grace of God working in her, Holofernes agreed with her and was silent, and then they brought her into her tent. Holofernes thought that what she was thinking of was the surrender of the city to him, but she was thinking of God, who would save her people by her hands. Perhaps Holofernes' trust in Judith's holiness, and that she was a prophetess of the gods, made him submit to her words, which came out of her mouth quietly but with great power.
