Do you have such trust in God, who protects you, surrounds you and saves you from any affliction, whatever the material obstacles? The strength of your faith silences the wicked, so that they do not resist you.

entries.section: (1) Judith's prayers and fasts in the camp of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: After Judith had surveyed the place of the tent and what was in it, she felt that it was suitable for her to stay in and to fulfil her worship in quiet, but that it was far from the springs of water that she needed for washing before completing her prayers, according to the Mosaic Law. So she asked Holofernes for permission to go down to the valley below the mountain on which her city stood, to wash there, since her tent, the tent of Holofernes, and the tents of his treasuries were on a hill above that valley. She asked this permission for three days only, as is understood from (v. 6), since she believed that God would intervene after that and save His people out of compassion for them, before the five days that they had set earlier, according to the divine revelation to which we referred (ch. 11:13). The period of three days points to the number of the Holy Trinity, that is, the perfection of the divine work, which is stronger and swifter than human striving, to which the number five points, in reference to human striving and the five Mosaic sacrifices. For the work of God is stronger and swifter than what the human heart imagines.

Judith's piety appears in her holding fast to prayer not only during the day but in the last watch, that is, the last part of the night, and then she continued praying throughout the day. She prayed night and day with fasting, asceticism and purification with water according to the Law. We note her exactness in washing: she did not wash with the water found among the Assyrians, but with the water of the springs belonging to her city. To this degree she was exact.

entries.section: (1) Judith's prayers and fasts in the camp of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: From the depth of Holofernes' admiration for Judith and his conviction of her connection with her God, he agreed without the slightest doubt about her, although the springs of water in which she would wash were close to her city, as appears from (v. 7).

Do not be ashamed to hold fast to the commandments of God, and to all that the fulfilment of those commandments requires. God will give you favor in the eyes of others and will prepare suitable circumstances for you to live with Him, even if the purposes of others differ and their thoughts are evil, far from God.

entries.section: (1) Judith's prayers and fasts in the camp of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: On the next day Judith began, in the early morning, to wash at the spring of water in the valley of Bethulia, then she would go up to her tent and continue prayer and fasting until evening, in tears, humility and supplication to God, as though she were in her upper room in her house continuing her devotional life and eating her ascetic food. Then she would pray and rest during the night, to wake on the following day... and so she continued her worship as though she were living in a monastery and not in the midst of the camp of the enemies.

How strong is your faith and your prayers, Judith, and your holding to fasting with all rigor! You put us to shame, we who are negligent, making excuses to God because of the circumstances, problems and pressures of life.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes invites Judith to spend the night with him

paragraphs.text: After the end of the three days that Judith spent in fasting, prayers and fervent worship, waiting for God to declare His will, the surprise came: Holofernes made a supper, that is, a banquet for his servants. Of course the servants meant here are his close officers, and not all his army, whose number was one hundred and fifty thousand soldiers. He held this banquet to express his joy at the near victory, and hoping to spend his night with Judith, whose captivating beauty had taken possession of his heart.

The difference appears clearly between the thinking of the children of God and the children of the world as they prepare for great deeds: the children of God take refuge in Him with fervent prayers and strong fasts, while the wicked are absorbed in their pleasures. Thus afflictions lead us to spiritual growth, while they lead the wicked to various sins. Holofernes sent his eunuch called "Bagoas" (he was the head of his private guard; the guard was chosen from eunuchs possessing bodily strength, so that Holofernes could enjoy himself and plunge into his lusts without fear of him concerning his women). This confirms the absorption of the wicked and their careful planning to satisfy their bodily pleasures and indulge in delights. He sent him in the evening to Judith, that she might agree to spend the night in his tent, with him on his bed, without using force or compulsion, since it is a disgrace and shame among the Assyrians for a woman to leave them without their lying with her.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes invites Judith to spend the night with him

paragraphs.text: So Bagoas went to her, in awe of her holiness and goodness, and told her of Holofernes' desire, asking her to agree without shame or refusal, since this is the usual and natural thing among the Assyrians. He encouraged her that her lying with Holofernes would give her great honor, to be one of his maidservants, so that she would eat and drink with him, that is, be among those nearest to him. Thus we see the extent of Holofernes' lust, matched by the chastity and holiness of Judith, and this is the reason for Holofernes' defeat, for he was defeated by his lust and by the chastity of Judith.

How strange are the thoughts of men! They not only fall into sins, but regard that as something ordinary and boast of it, and purity and uprightness have become shame and disgrace. To such a degree does the devil control their lives and thoughts. So beware lest your thoughts mix with theirs, lest you be polluted or lose some of your principles, and then justify your sins and thus close upon yourself the door of repentance, since you have become permissive.

entries.section: (2) Holofernes invites Judith to spend the night with him

paragraphs.text: Good: he sees it as good.

It was an extremely difficult situation for Judith. Would she hold fast to her purity and refuse to submit to the pressing desires and lusts of Holofernes, which were for him something logical and natural? Or would she agree and give up her purity? ... Nothing helped her in this critical situation except her prayers and worship over the three days, and indeed what had preceded that in her house.

We believe that God's earlier revelation to her of the details of her secret mission, and that Holofernes would ask her to spend the night with him, kept her from being astonished at Bagoas' request, so she agreed with all welcome and humility, expressing that it was a great honor for her, in which she would take pride all her life. This is a high degree of faith that surpasses reason, so that she became a symbol of the Virgin Mary, who agreed to be betrothed to the one the priests would choose, to live in his house, while she longed to be a virgin, and because of her faith that bewilders minds, God indeed chose for her St. Joseph the carpenter, the aged man, who would care for her while she kept her virginity.

It is noticed that at the end of her words about Holofernes she said, "Whatever pleases him, that will be very good to me all the days of my life." She sees in Holofernes' sensual, evil desire the means God uses to complete His plan to deliver His people from the hand of the Assyrians, so she continues to glorify God all the days of her life, who used this evil desire. For God's plan is always good and worthy of glory.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: After Judith's agreement to Bagoas, she put on beautiful, shining garments and adorned herself with all her adornment, as she had done three days before at the first meeting with Holofernes.

She prepared with her maidservant supper food for the two of them, and they went with Bagoas to the great tent of Holofernes. Bagoas went in and told Holofernes of Judith's coming to him, and he rejoiced greatly. Then she was brought in to him in his bedchamber, and her maidservant remained with some guards and officers in the outer reception room. When he saw her he was dazzled by her beauty, and his lusts were stirred violently and strongly, for he had longed to see her this night.

These were terrible moments through which Judith passed. She had no helper except God who dwelt in her, who supported her and gave her strength, steadfastness and irresistible beauty to accomplish His will.

Be sure, my brother, that when people leave you, you will feel the help of God, whom you seek more than at any other time, and He increases you in strength and gives you favor in the eyes of others, even if they want to do you harm.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Favor: a distinguished standing.

After Bagoas departed, Judith was standing alone before Holofernes, who was sitting on his bed, and he said to her, "Sit down now and eat and drink, for I admire you, and you have found favor in my eyes." Judith obeyed, with all steadfastness, confidence, gentleness and humility before Holofernes, giving him to eat and drink first, and declaring her deep joy on this great day, the like of which she had not known in all her days. She meant, of course, that with the eye of faith she saw the salvation of God that would be accomplished by her hands, by destroying this man and rescuing her people. But this wicked man, in the excess of his pride, did not doubt her admiration for him, and that she felt proud to accompany him and to spend the night with him.
Beware of pride, for it blinds the eyes of a person, so that his thoughts are deceived and he loses his wisdom, and indeed his whole life.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Then she went out to the reception room, took pieces of fleece and spread them on the ground (as mentioned in the translation of the Jesuit Fathers), and set out the food and drink that her maidservant had prepared for her (as the Jewish law allows), and sat down to eat and drink. Of course the wine she had brought with her was grape juice, only lightly fermented, not intoxicating, and not causing a person to lose consciousness, although it looked to Holofernes like any wine.
Holofernes allowed her to eat her food and drink her drink, as we mentioned before, out of the excess of his admiration for her, because of the grace of God working in her.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Before her: near her and facing her.

As for him, his joy increased at her being with him, and as he was reassured by her obedience to him and her sitting before him in a gentle manner, eating and drinking, the fires of lust blazed in him violently. He lost his balance and began to drink without awareness, in large quantities, as he had never done in all his life. Judith was very beautiful, and God increased her beauty in his eyes and put into his heart a sense of safety from her, and he lost control over himself and went on drinking without restraint.

How did Holofernes rush to drink wine to this degree? What drove him but his evil lusts and the corruption of his impure heart? God permitted this so that his evil would come upon his own head, and that He might deliver His people from his hands.

The sin of the sinner comes upon his own head before it touches others. So let us hasten to repentance, to protect ourselves from sin and receive forgiveness in the sacrament of confession, and to protect others from our harming them by our sin.
The killing of Holofernes and the escape of Judith (1) The cutting off of Holofernes' head (vv. 1-10)

1- And when evening came, his servants made haste to their homes, and Bagoas closed the doors of the bedchamber and went away. 2- They were all weighed down with wine. 3- And Judith was alone in the bedchamber. 4- And Holofernes was lying on the bed asleep, because of his great drunkenness. 5- And Judith commanded her maidservant to stand outside before the bedchamber and keep watch.

6- And Judith stood before the bed, and she was praying with tears and moving her lips in silence. 7- And she said, Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, and look in this hour upon the work of my hands, that Jerusalem Your city may rise up as You promised, and that I may accomplish what I have resolved, trusting that I can do it by Your help. 8- And when she had said this she came near to the pillar that was at the head of his bed, and loosed his dagger that hung there tied to it. 9- And she drew it, and took hold of the hair of his head, and said, Strengthen me, O Lord God, in this hour. 10- Then she struck twice upon his neck and cut off his head, and pulled down the canopy of his bed from the pillars, and rolled his body off the bed.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: After Bagoas had performed his task and succeeded in easily bringing Judith willingly to the bedchamber of his master, and the minutes passed quietly while he heard from afar the whispers of conversation between his master and Judith, he dismissed the private guard of Holofernes' tent, who had begun to drink in celebration of this night in which their master had granted them the right to revelry and carousing, while he himself enjoyed the company of the beautiful Judith.

Perhaps Judith confirmed the permission she had received to wash at the springs of Bethulia at the end of the night, before dawn, so she asked Bagoas' leave, saying that after spending the night with Holofernes she would go as usual to wash at the springs of water beside her city "Bethulia." He allowed her and informed the guards of the camp of this. Then Bagoas felt that there was no need for his presence and that it was better to leave his master in his seclusion with Judith. So he closed the door of the tent upon them, left Judith's maidservant in the reception room, and departed, to enjoy for himself also the delicious food and abundant drink at the banquet.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Judith found herself alone in the bedchamber of Holofernes, who, from drinking so much wine, had thrown himself on his bed and sunk into a deep sleep.

Wonderful are Your plans, O Lord! You prepared for Your servant Judith everything that would help her to perform her mission. You made Holofernes, out of the intensity of his admiration for her, drink to excess and far exceed the amount he was accustomed to drink, so he lost consciousness completely and slept deeply. As for his soldiers, they were busy with revelry, drunkenness and eating, and forgot their caution and left their guarding of the tent. Even Bagoas, You put reassurance in his heart, so he too went away to the banquet, leaving his master unguarded, confident that he was immersed in his pleasures with the beautiful Judith.

Advance in your spiritual practices of prayers, fasts and readings, and also in serving God with enthusiasm, confident that God will help you and arrange everything to fulfil His will in you, because He desires your salvation more than you desire it, and He Himself is the One who works in the service, while you are merely an instrument to share with Him the joy of the salvation of the souls of others.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Watch: keep an eye out.

When Judith found the enemy of God fallen in deep sleep, with God having prepared for her all the means and the atmosphere entirely clear for her, she went out and made sure herself that her maidservant was sitting alone in the reception room, that there was not a single guard at the door, and that everyone had disappeared inside the tents, eating, drinking and revelling. She commanded her maidservant to stand beside the outer door of the tent and to listen carefully for any sound or approaching footsteps. Although God had arranged everything, Judith did her duty with exactness and complete caution, not relying idly on Him. Although God alone is able to kill and destroy Holofernes, she must do her duty fully. So too Christ was able to raise Lazarus, yet they had first to remove the stone.

Do not be negligent in your spiritual striving, in your prayers, fasts and readings, and leave no gap for sin to enter you. Then God will fulfil His will in you, and Satan your enemy will fall prostrate under your feet.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Then Judith entered the bedchamber a second time, with Holofernes lying before her on his bed, and she lifted her eyes toward heaven in a prayer from the depth of the heart. Her voice was not heard in it, but it appeared in the moving of her lips and her tears flowing down her cheeks, as she asked God in the most critical moment of her life. Here appears the extent of her humility, her feeling of weakness and need of God, and her trust in His power that supported her. There was not a single atom of a feeling of reliance on herself, on her own person and her beauty, in this service, but her reliance was wholly on God.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Rise up: rescue, raise and lift up His people from their humiliation.

She reminded Him that He is the God of Israel and that His city is Jerusalem, and asked Him to fulfil His promises to protect His children. Let Him bless her work now with the salvation of His people, to be rid of Holofernes their enemy, for she believed that His power was able to help her to accomplish her difficult mission with which God had charged her.
God rejoices when you ask Him to fulfil His promises, declare your sonship to Him and your holding to Him alone, and press Him to save you from all your sins and troubles.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: His dagger: it was the custom of kings and chiefs to hang a weapon by their beds to defend themselves, and this dagger was not an ordinary dagger but resembled a small sword, to befit the rank of its owner.
Drew it: took it out of its sheath.
The canopy of his bed: the mosquito net, a large cloth covering that covers the bed, placed on its four posts, to keep insects off those lying on the bed.

After this Judith stepped forward, her strong faith having given her extraordinary courage to accomplish a very difficult mission, contrary to her gentle nature, since she had spent her whole life in quiet inside her house, and after her widowhood she had devoted herself to prayers and meditations.

God gives strength to accomplish His work, even if it is strange and contrary to the nature of the person who performs it, as Jeremiah, who had delicate feelings, rebuked his people and all the rulers, shepherds and priests, and likewise David, the ruddy youth with beautiful eyes, who killed a lion and a bear and Goliath the giant.

The decisive moment drew near, and Judith looked at the head of the bed and found the dagger of Holofernes hanging, tied to the post of the bed, on the side of Holofernes' head. She untied it and held it in her right hand, and stretched out her left hand courageously and took hold of the hair of Holofernes and lifted it from the pillow, while he was sunk in his sleep, completely unconscious. She lifted her heart in a prayer seeking God's help, that He might support her with His power in this terrible moment, and with all her strength she struck his neck from behind twice, and separated his head from his body, and his blood flowed abundantly.

After that she threw the dagger from her, and with her right hand pulled down the canopy of Holofernes' bed and wrapped his head in it, and set it to one side. Then she rolled his body off the bed and let it down to the ground. Thus the mighty man fell at the feet of Judith, as Satan falls under the feet of the striving children of God. Judith here is a type of Christ, who triumphed over Satan by the Cross.

The killing here is not a crime, because it is self-defense. She is rescuing herself and her people from Holofernes the tyrant, who came to besiege the city and kill those in it, and killing is permitted in wars, because it is self-defense. Holofernes dies by his own dagger. Instead of killing the children of God with this dagger, he is killed by it. Thus God delivers His children, while the evil of the wicked comes upon their own heads.

Here Judith shines in the Holy Bible above many of the heroes who killed enemies. Ehud, who killed Eglon (Judg 3:20-22), was a man of war, but Judith, the gentle woman, received extraordinary strength from God that made her braver than men of war. And Jael, who killed Sisera (Judg 4:
17-22) did so with Sisera, who was fleeing and hiding in her tent in fear, but Judith was in the midst of the camp of the enemies, with no weapon but the power of God.

Do not make peace with sin, but cut it off with all force, and confirm your cutting it off more than once. Separate the head of the serpent from its body, and cut off its head, to be rid of its poisons, that is, to be rid of the main source of sin. Be strong and take courage, for by the power of your God you can overcome the devil, and he will be humbled at your feet.
(2) Judith's arrival at her city and her proclaiming of the good news (vv. 11-21)
11- And after a little while she went out and handed her maidservant the head of Holofernes and commanded her to put it in her bag.

12- And the two of them went out according to their custom, as though going out to pray, and passed through the camp and went around the valley until they came to the gate of the city. 13- And Judith cried out from afar to the keepers of the wall, Open the gates, for God is with us, and has shown power in Israel. 14- And when the men heard her voice, they called the elders of the city. 15- And they all hastened to her, from the least of them to the greatest, for they had not hoped that she would return. 16- Then they lit lamps and gathered around her, all of them, and she went up to the highest place and commanded silence, and when they were all silent,

17- Judith said, Praise the Lord our God, who has not forsaken those who trust in Him. 18- And by me His handmaid He has fulfilled His mercy which He promised to the house of Israel, and has slain by my hand the enemy of His people this night. 19- Then she took the head of Holofernes out of the bag and showed it, saying, Behold the head of Holofernes, the chief of the army of the Assyrians, and this is the canopy of his bed in which he lay in his drunkenness, where the Lord our God smote him by the hand of a woman. 20- As the Lord liveth, He hath kept me by His angel in my going from here and in my staying there and in my coming back here, and the Lord did not permit His handmaid to be defiled, but brought me back to you without the stain of sin, rejoicing in His victory and my deliverance and yours. 21- Give thanks to Him, all of you, for He is good, for His mercy endureth for ever.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: A little while: a few moments.
Her bag: a cloth sack in which she carried food.
Judith looked at the body lying on the ground and the head wrapped in the canopy of the bed, and she stood for a short time thanking God, contemplating with wonder and pride the great work of God.

Then she hurried to complete her task. She took up the head wrapped in the canopy of the bed, and lifted the curtain of the tent that separates the bedchamber from the place of reception, and found her maidservant alone. She asked her to open her bag in which she had brought the food, and she put the head of Holofernes in it.

Here appears the role of Judith's maidservant, who accompanied her in this difficult mission, and who had probably been close to her throughout the years of her widowhood, sharing her prayers, her fasts and her worship. Judith had chosen her because she trusted her, because she worshipped God faithfully and because she kept secrets. Perhaps Judith had disclosed to her some of the steps of this mission, and the maidservant shared with Judith the three days of prayers and fasts while she was with Holofernes; perhaps the two of them encouraged one another, remembering the power of God and His care for His people. Then the decisive moment came, and the maidservant stood watching and observing those who passed around the tent from a distance, full of faith in the power of God who was keeping them. Now, with a strong heart, she faced the work of God and the success of her mistress in cutting off the head of Holofernes. She was not shaken, but opened her bag to put the head of this wicked man in it. She went out with Judith, reached Bethulia, and shared with her in bringing the good news of God's victory to her people, and she continued to share her mistress's worship and life of solitude all her days. Because of the greatness of her faith, Judith set her free, yet she continued to enjoy Judith's companionship all her days. She is an example of the spiritual servant who cares for spiritual discipleship and obedience, so that her faith grows and she rises to high spiritual levels.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Then the two of them went out of the tent and found no one, for everyone was either busy eating or weighed down with drink inside their tents. They passed between the tents until they reached the end of the camp, and went down into the valley leading to Bethulia. Perhaps some of the guards at the edge of the camp saw them, but no one suspected them, since they were used to seeing them go out to bathe at the springs of water near Bethulia during the previous three days, in addition to Bagoas' order to allow them to bathe this night also. Then they continued on their way and disappeared from the sight of the soldiers, until they reached the gates of the city.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Then Judith called to the keepers of the gate and to those on the wall of the city, saying to them:
Open the gates, for our God has done a great work.
God, who was glorified by the hand of this woman, weak in body and strong in faith, is of course able to complete His work, so that no one will stop them or suspect them.

If you have conquered the devil in your struggle and have left some sin, do not let the devil make you doubt, suggesting the possibility of falling again; rather be strong and take courage, and complete your striving until you reach the gates of the great city in which the children of God dwell, Bethulia, which points to the heavenly Jerusalem. Then you will be able to call to the keepers, as the angels called - those who ascended with the Spirit of the victorious Christ, who bound the devil on the Cross - to the keepers of Paradise, which had been closed for ages before man, to open so that the Son of Man, Christ our God, might enter as the representative of all humanity, opening and preparing the way after Him for all who believe in Him; and they said, "Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in" (Ps 24:7). The head of Holofernes, who was proud and exalted himself over all the nations, indeed over God and His people Israel, and destroyed many with might and tyranny, and cast peoples far from their cities, is carried by a weak maidservant in her bag, that is, her sack.

Do not be proud of your strength and of what you have achieved, and do not boast over others, lest God's longsuffering toward you come to an end and you be humbled and carried where you do not wish, by the hand of the one who seems weakest to you.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: All of them: everyone.

The gatekeepers and the guards of the walls were astonished when they heard the voice of Judith, for they had given up hope of her return. They had thought that she had undertaken a reckless adventure and that she would surely perish or become one of the enemy's slave girls. When they were certain that it was Judith and her maidservant, they hurried to open the gates and received her with great joy.

They hurried to call the elders of the city to meet her. The elders woke up and the news spread throughout the whole city, and all the people ran hastily to the city square, asking eagerly about what she had done with the Assyrians, how she had returned, and what the Assyrians had done to her. They brought torches to light the place, and Judith went up to a high place with her maid beside her, and signaled to everyone to be silent. They fell silent, longing to know what had happened at her hands: had she been able to reach an understanding with the enemies, or had she failed and escaped from their hands in disappointment, especially as thirst had overcome them, for this was the fourth day and only one day remained of the delay they had set for Uzziah, the ruler of the city, to surrender the city before they died of thirst. This is the Church gathered around the servants of God to hear His word, and the servant, whom Judith signifies, stands to give the joyful good news to all the people. Judith also signifies Christ, who triumphed over the devil and rose from the dead, proclaiming salvation to everyone who believes in Him; for Judith triumphed over Holofernes, and she is now proclaiming to her city their deliverance from the enemies.

Do you bring joyful good news to all around you? If you are striving on the way with God, you will experience His work, and then you will be able to encourage all around you by the grace and power of God. The opposite is also true: if you are harsh in your speech and do not encourage those around you, you have not yet known the way of spiritual striving.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Judith called all the people to thank God and praise Him, because He did not forsake His children who trust in Him, however great their weakness and the strength of their enemies, but He supports and rescues all who believe in Him.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Then she continued speaking with great humility, declaring that she was not a courageous heroine but a weak handmaid, by whose hand God, out of His love and humility, accomplished His mercy toward His people in Bethulia, and indeed in all Judea. This is the mercy that He promised them by the mouth of His prophets and His saints.

Here appears the humility of Judith, who did not ascribe any glory to herself in this great victory, but ascribed faith and trust in God to all the people, although the faith of the people was weak and they wanted to surrender the city; it was she who made them stop by the strength of her faith, and because of this certainty God gave them the victory.

The greatest power that overthrows Satan is humility, so that God is glorified and the devil is defeated. Hold fast to humility during your striving, and after your victory, when you thank God and encourage the hearts of those around you.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Then she announced the great news that God had destroyed Holofernes by her hand. She looked at her maidservant and took out of her bag the head of Holofernes, wrapped in the canopy of his bed, and held it by the hair and raised it before them, saying: This is the head of Holofernes, the chief of the army of the Assyrians. She told them how he perished, when he indulged in drink until he was drunk and lost consciousness and lay down on his bed, and she cut off his head and took the canopy of his bed and wrapped it in it. Thus God destroyed this great commander by the hand of a weak woman, and she affirmed her humility a second time and ascribed the glory to God; for a woman overcoming a man and killing him is regarded as something strange because of the physical strength of man, how much more so when a weak woman kills the commander of a great army while he is in his camp and among his soldiers.

Give those around you the proof of the truth of your good news. The proof is the devil humbled under your feet: his head is cut off, that is, he has no power, through your holding fast to virtue, purity, truthfulness and faithfulness. Let the devil have no authority over you, and let sin be humbled under your feet. That is, be an example and a joyful good news to every person, always directing thanks and glory to God for the good conduct He has granted you, which rises above the conduct of the world around you.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: My return: my coming back.

Then Judith continued her good news to all the people, that is, to the Church, and to all of us. She said that, by human reasoning, for this victory to be accomplished by the hand of a beautiful woman, she would have to pass through thousands of strong, wicked men who would capture her, and stay with them for three days, and even enter the bedchamber of a mighty, powerful man immersed in drinking wine; she would surely be harmed and exposed to terrifying dangers, and would of necessity be violated and lose her purity. But the mighty God sent His angel from the time she left her city, Bethulia, and he walked with her all along her way, and even stayed with her and kept her in all her meetings with the wicked, even in the bedchamber of this wicked man, so that no one touched her with harm, nor was her purity stained. Thus Judith achieved in her difficult mission three victories:
1- Her keeping her purity among lustful wicked men, by the keeping of God's angel.
2- The killing of the chief of the enemy's armies, and consequently the spreading of terror afterward in the hearts of his army, so that they fled.
3- The rescue of her people from destruction, and even their seizing very many spoils.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: She asked them to rejoice with her in the salvation of the Lord and to glorify Him, because He magnified His work toward them and kept her and kept them; He is truly good, and His mercy endures for ever. This wonderful hymn is repeated in Psalm 135, which the Church recites in her daily praise and which is called the Second Hoos, or the Second Praise.

God is able not only to solve your problems in the midst of affliction in peace, but to bring you out of it purer, cleaner and more loving toward God, so that you are purified from your sins and become more closely bound to God. Then do not forget to lift up praise and thanksgiving to God; rather, make your prayer a daily praise before Him for His former works with you.

Do not be afraid to undertake difficult services if the necessity is laid upon you, and trust that God's angel will keep you and make you succeed, and will save many souls by your hands, and will save you first, so that you rejoice and praise God.
(3) Glorifying of Judith by the people and Achior (vv. 22-31)
22- And they all worshipped the Lord and said to her, The Lord has blessed you by His power, for by you He has brought our enemies to nothing.

23- And Uzziah, the ruler of the people of Israel, said to her, Blessed art thou, daughter, of the Lord God Most High above all the women upon the earth. 24- Blessed be the Lord God, who created the heavens and the earth, who directed thy hand to the cutting off of the head of the chief of our enemies.

25- For this day He has so magnified thy name that thy praise shall not depart from the mouths of men who remember the power of the Lord for ever, for whose sake thou hast not spared thy life, because of the affliction and distress of thy race, but hast turned away destruction before our God.

26- And all the people said, So be it, so be it. 27- Then they called Achior, and he came, and Judith said to him, The God of Israel, to whom thou hast borne witness that He avenges Himself of His enemies, has cut off this night by my hand the head of all the unbelievers. 28- And that thou mayest know that it is so, behold the head of Holofernes, who despised the God of Israel in the arrogance of his pride, and threatened thee with death, saying, When the people of Israel are taken, I will command that they pierce thy sides with the sword. 29- When Achior saw the head of Holofernes, he was seized with terror and fell on his face on the ground, and his soul was troubled. 30- And after his spirit returned to him and he was revived, he fell down before her, worshipping her, and said, 31- Blessed art thou by thy God in all the tents of Jacob, and in every nation which shall hear of thy name, the God of Israel shall be magnified because of thee.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: When the people heard this joyful news, they rejoiced and were glad, just as the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord Christ in the upper room after His resurrection from the dead, victorious. So Judith signified Christ risen from the dead.
Then they expressed their thanks and submission to God by all bowing down before Him, as the twenty-four elders bow down before God in the heavenly Jerusalem.
And after they had blessed God, they glorified Judith also, because God blessed her, worked in her by His power and destroyed their enemies by her.
God is glorified in His saints, and He is ready to bless you and work through you, if you humble yourself, submit to Him and hold fast to your faith in Him.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: In the same way Uzziah, the ruler of the city, spoke on behalf of the people, blessing Judith from the Lord and exalting her above all the women of the earth, because there is no faith like this in all the world.
If you have faith, God will be glorified through you, and in proportion to your faith the work of the Lord is magnified in you and through you.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Directed thy hand: held thy hand and aimed it to strike Holofernes, or used thy hand to kill him.

Then Uzziah glorified God, who strengthened this weak woman to kill the greatest and fiercest of the world's brave men at that time - Holofernes - the enemy of the people of God, who wanted to destroy them. The truth is that what defeated Holofernes was his evil lusts, and what sustained Judith was her chastity and her trust in God, so that He worked through her with power and gave her victory for the sake of her purity, as St. Jerome pointed out. The power of God is above every power, and He is able to work the greatest works through a weak human being, as He was born of the humble Virgin, being God incarnate; as all Jerusalem submitted to John the Baptist, who had stripped himself of everything in the wilderness; and as God overcame tens of thousands of enemies by Gideon and the three hundred men.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Uzziah declared that on this day the name of Judith is joined to the names of the prophets and the holy men of God, so that all the faithful may remember them with glory and honor throughout the generations, because she is a living example of sacrifice, courage and strength of faith, for she threw herself into the camp of the enemies for the sake of God and the rescue of her people; so God was glorified through her and turned evil and destruction away from His people.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: When the people heard the words of Uzziah, they declared their agreement with all that he said, saying, Amen, Amen.

How beautiful it is to bless God and glorify Him, and how great to praise Him in His saints and recall His works in them throughout the past generations. Strengthen yourself with praise, and you will grow stronger in your spiritual striving. Take part in the praise of the Church, to join the procession of the heroes who strive and triumph over sin.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: Achior the Ammonite was not present among them at the time when they rejoiced at the good news of Judith. So they sent for him and brought him, and he came quickly, for he had learned of Judith's return, and his heart was filled with fear and joy when he saw the crowd of people in the square and Judith standing on a high platform in their midst. As soon as he reached Judith, she said to him that the God of Israel, to whose power thou didst bear witness before Holofernes, and whose power no man can resist, had been glorified this day by my hand, for He cut off the head of all the wicked who stood against the people of God, since Holofernes was the head and chief of all the armies of the Assyrians.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: And Holofernes, who insulted God, the God of Israel, and made light of His power, affirming his victory over God and His people and his seizing of Bethulia and indeed all Judea, and who would then have seized thee and killed thee in the most terrible manner by piercing thy sides with his sword - this Holofernes, God has cut off his head by my hand.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: His soul was troubled: his soul was greatly disturbed.

She showed him the head of Holofernes. Achior, who knew him well, had never imagined seeing this head, so lofty and haughty toward everyone, in such humiliation and disgrace, held up by its hair in the hand of a woman. So he was struck with great fear before the power of God at the hands of Judith, and fell on his face and lost consciousness from the excess of his fear.

If you are a powerful ruler with authority, or a father who shepherds his household, do not rush ahead in pride, whatever your position, threatening those beneath you with your authority and lording it over them; rather fear God with humility, lest He humble you. And be sure, believer and servant, that God will show forth your right, however much the wicked oppose you, make light of you and threaten you, warning you of evil. Stand firm on the promises and the word of God, and He will keep you.

entries.section: (3) Judith in the tent of Holofernes and his drinking of wine

paragraphs.text: His spirit returned to him: his spirit came back to him, that is, he recovered from his fainting.

The tents of Jacob: an expression common at that time, meaning all the people of Israel, who lived in tents for forty years in the wilderness of Sinai, and like Jacob their father, who lived in a tent all his life.

Achior recovered from his fainting, turned toward Judith and bowed down before her, declaring his submission to God, bearing witness to her holiness and the great strength of her faith, and declaring that from this day she would be honored and her standing great among all the people of God, and indeed among the peoples of the world who would hear her story and glorify God because of her life and her faith.

Does your life glorify God, bear witness to Him and draw many souls to Him, even those far from the faith? God is ready to give you spiritual dignity in the eyes of all, so that they bow before you and honor you and glorify God in you.
The terror of the Assyrians at the death of their commander

entries.section: (1) Judith's offensive plan

paragraphs.text: Judith continued her speech by laying out a plan for the salvation of her people. She was not content with strengthening their faith, then sacrificing herself to destroy Holofernes, then proclaiming his death to them; now she gives them guidance as a military commander on how to attack the Assyrians and finish them off.

She is a symbol of the Church, which confirms faith through her Holy Sacraments, overthrows Satan by the Cross of her Christ, leads us in spiritual striving through the various spiritual practices, and teaches us through her saints how to triumph over Satan.

Her plan was based, first, on hanging the head of Holofernes on the wall of the city. This is a strong psychological motive, confirming that the victory has been accomplished by her hand, so that the fighting soldiers trust that the victory begun by the hand of Judith will be completed by their striving in the power of God. Likewise the Church hangs the Cross on high before the eyes of the faithful as proof of Christ's victory over Satan, and so urges her children to strive against the wars of the devil.

Do not rejoice in your first victory over Satan; rather, for your victory to be completed and to be a true victory, you must continue your striving. The cutting off of the head of Holofernes had to be completed by attacking the Assyrians, to drive them completely away from Judea; that is, you must continue to pursue every evil thought and everything related to sin, so that all your senses are purified. Your striving continues throughout your life, and you will rejoice in the full crown of victory in the Kingdom. For the devil exploits your sense of security and your somewhat lax state after your first victory, to fight you fiercely. So be watchful in order to overcome him, and trust that God supports you to defeat him.

entries.section: (1) Judith's offensive plan

paragraphs.text: The second step in the plan is that they take up their weapons at sunrise and go down from the city, but not quietly like fugitives, or like infiltrators stealing a little water, but with force and loud voices. Thus the Assyrians, whose officers have not yet recovered from the drunkenness and revelry of the previous night, will be taken by surprise by the sight of the army of the Jews, with their swords gleaming in the light of the sun, the mighty voices and the fearsome charge, and they will be confused, alarmed and even terrified.

May you attack the devil with your spiritual weapons, which are prayers, the Holy Bible, the sacraments of the Church and every spiritual practice, so that his soldiers are alarmed and are defeated before you. Let your war be at sunrise, early, and you will find God, and He will give you victory over the devil with ease. Do not be afraid of the devil, but attack him with all courage. St. Anba Anthony spoke truly when he said: "The demons are cowards, and they attack only cowards like themselves."

entries.section: (1) Judith's offensive plan

paragraphs.text: Judith told the men of war that if they attacked the Assyrians, their spies who were watching the city of Bethulia would hasten to inform the commanders of the army, who would run to the tent of Holofernes and find him slain. Then the Assyrians would be terrified to find their great, mighty commander, who was thought impossible to kill, slaughtered in the midst of his guards, and they would flounder like sheep without a shepherd, and would hasten to flee from before you.

entries.section: (1) Judith's offensive plan

paragraphs.text: Then she charged them to pursue the Assyrians and run after them, so that they would flee and then be quickly defeated, afraid of the Jews, and she strengthened their faith so that they would follow them up and drive them far away from their land. From this precise plan, in addition to what Judith did with Holofernes and what was mentioned in the previous chapters, we understand that she had certainly seen all this by divine revelation, which encouraged her, and it was her faith that supported her to carry out God's plan, especially since the plan she has just mentioned was fulfilled in all its details - as will appear in the following verses. This confirms that she speaks with the voice of God, confident of what she saw and heard from God. She is like Moses the prophet, who spoke with God, and God gave him not only the commandments and the Law but also the design of the tabernacle in its precise details, and he carried it out according to the pattern he had seen.

When you raise the Cross before the wars of the demons, you show them their chief, the devil, bound by the Cross, so they fear and flee from you. So continue in your striving, pursuing them, to drive them out of all your thoughts and senses, and far away from all who are around you, through your service and your care for the souls around you. Trust that God is with you; so be strong and complete your striving, to triumph over them and drive them far away.

entries.section: (1) Judith's offensive plan

paragraphs.text: His foreskin: that is, his uncircumcision; what is meant is that he was circumcised.
The custom of the Gentiles: idol worship.

Before the mighty work of God by the hand of Judith, Achior felt that there is no god but Him, because He had overcome the strongest personality in the world at that time, Holofernes. So he declared his faith in the God of Israel, and reminded the elders of Bethulia of their promise to him to receive him with them into the faith. He asked to become a Jew like them and to be circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, declaring by the cutting of his flesh that he would cut off idol worship and all the evils of the Gentiles, and that he would live in purity and uprightness before God. After the victory over the Assyrians, he brought his family from the children of Ammon, and he and his household joined the people of the Jews.

The power of God at the hands of the saints draws the souls of those who are far off, so that they declare their faith and leave their evils, being baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, they and their households, as happened in the days of the Apostles.

Most people are moved by powerful events, such as the wonderful works of God in His saints and His miracles, but few are those who turn their emotional response into faith and faith into deeds. Achior, being moved by what he saw by the hand of Judith, declared his faith, was circumcised and joined the Jews, he and his household. It is not enough for you to be moved by the stories of the saints; you need to strive as they did and follow their example.

entries.section: (2) The discovery of the killing of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: When the day broke: when the day lit up, that is, at dawn.
Uproar: a great noise.

The men of Bethulia carried out the words of their military leader Judith with great precision. At dawn, when the light of day appeared, they hung the head on the wall, then took their weapons and rushed against the camp of the Assyrians with shouting and a great uproar.

entries.section: (2) The discovery of the killing of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: The spies of the Assyrians hurried to the tent of Holofernes and told the guards of the tent what had happened. But none of them could go in to wake him, or even clap before his tent, because of his greatness and tyranny. So they made a noise and began to speak in loud voices at the door of the tent, hoping that he would wake up, so that they might tell him what had happened.

The blessing of obedience is very great, and the humble carry it out with all precision. So did the men of Bethulia, and the events followed one another as Judith had told them. May you be obedient to the Church, to your father of confession and to your spiritual guides, so that you succeed in your spiritual wars and see with your own eyes what God has promised you. Holofernes, this arrogant man whom no one dared to wake, lies on the ground, drowned in his blood, his head taken off him. Bow your head in humility, and God will lift you up; but if you exalt yourself, He will crush you, as the Virgin said in her hymn: "He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree" (Lk 1:52).

entries.section: (2) The discovery of the killing of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: The chamberlains: the personal guards.
Their confinement: from "confinement," the meaning being the siege in which the city of Bethulia had been placed by the Assyrians.

The news spread quickly among the tents of the Assyrians, especially among the commanders of the armies. All the senior officers of the army gathered before the tent of Holofernes and noticed that the loud voices which the guards were making did not wake Holofernes. With the mentality of guardsmen, they ordered the guards to go in and wake Holofernes so that he might act quickly in the face of this attack coming from Bethulia. Their pride clearly appears, for they described the Jews not as despised human beings, nor even as animals, but as mice that had come out of their confinement; and they did not say "to attack us," but "to provoke us," that is, to try to stir us up, that we might perhaps be willing to fight them.

They commanded that Holofernes be awakened, but how can one wake the one who has drowned, whom lust made lose his head, and who has fallen to the ground with his blood flowing? This is the man absorbed in the lusts of the world: he cannot hear the voice of God and be roused from his evil, because he has sunk down to material lusts, so he does not wake up, while he is dying every day without knowing it.
Do not despise others if you are strong, and do not exalt yourself because of your abilities, lest your shame appear and God humble you by the weakest of His children.

entries.section: (2) The discovery of the killing of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Stained: smeared.
He wailed: he cried out in grief.

At the orders of the commanders of the armies, the chief of the guards of the tent of Holofernes - Bagoas the eunuch - went into the reception room, adorned with gold and precious stones, but it was empty, with no one in it. He stood before the cloth curtain that separates the reception room from the bedchamber (the curtain), and heard no sound. He thought that Holofernes, after fulfilling his desire with Judith, had fallen asleep with her, so he was ashamed, and also afraid to go in on them.

Because of the tension of the situation, he was forced to disobey the orders of Holofernes by clapping his hands, but no one answered him. He began to suspect that his master was ill or in some distress, so he was forced to lift the curtain and enter the bedchamber. And the surprise came: the body of the strongest man in the world, lying on the ground without a head, and blood around it. He could not control his nerves; he cried out with a great and sorrowful voice and tore his clothes in dread and terror.

entries.section: (2) The discovery of the killing of Holofernes

paragraphs.text: Had thrown into confusion: shook them and made them troubled.

Then he went out quickly, with the eyes of the guards and the commanders of the armies watching him eagerly, and he entered the tent of Judith, pitched beside the tent of Holofernes, and found no one in it. By this he was certain that Judith was the killer of Holofernes. He went out to all the commanders and guards who had gathered, disturbed and eager to know what Holofernes had said, and announced to them that Judith the Hebrew had shaken the Assyrian empire and made it tremble, for she had killed the chief of the armies of the Assyrians, and behold, his body lay headless on the ground in his bedchamber.

If you do not heed God's warnings to you, you will be surprised by death before your eyes and will cry out in great fear. Let no one despise your youth or your weakness, for God is able to work through you, like Judith, so that He shakes the greatest nation in the world and subdues under your hands all the powers of evil.

entries.section: (3) The fear of the Assyrians

paragraphs.text: When the commanders of the armies heard the news of the killing of Holofernes, it was like a thunderbolt on their hearts. They were terrified, tore their clothes and trembled, for the news was beyond their imagination and conception, and they stood afraid and stunned. Meanwhile the news spread quickly among the tents of the Assyrians, and they were all alarmed and wept with loud cries, not only for the great Holofernes, but for themselves, for they expected destruction like his, by the hand of the God of Israel, whom none can resist, as Achior had told them before.

Where is the strength of the strong? It has collapsed before the power of God. Truly, "the Lord shall have them in derision, and vex them in His sore displeasure, and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel" (Ps 2:4, 5, 9).

You can escape terror before God the just Judge through repentance. Instead of weeping without hope at the end of days, offer the tears of repentance and enjoy God's forgiveness in the sacrament of confession.
The pursuit of the Assyrians and the plundering of their spoils

entries.section: (1) The pursuit of the fleeing Assyrians

paragraphs.text: They sought help in defeat: accepting defeat became a rescue for them, so that they might flee from the children of Israel and not be killed like their commander.

When the news of the killing of Holofernes reached the soldiers of the Assyrians, they lost all ability to think, fear settled in their hearts, and they felt weak and defeated before the God of Israel.

entries.section: (1) The pursuit of the fleeing Assyrians

paragraphs.text: While they were afraid and stunned, they bowed their heads in fear and humiliation, and found nothing to say to one another, from the horror of the surprise. When they heard the voice of the Jews coming against them, with their weapons gleaming in their hands, their terror increased. So they fled, leaving behind all their baggage, their tents, their sheep, their cattle and all their possessions, and hurried into the surrounding deserts, taking refuge in all the winding roads between the hills, hoping they might hide them from the face of the people of God. Perhaps the disturbing surprise made them stumble about, and opinions and orders conflicted, so that they scattered without order; some of them may even have fallen dead by the hand of a brother, or been trampled under foot. "Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?" (Ps 139:7). The Assyrians fled from the face of God, but His people overtook them. They killed many of them, and many fell on the way from exhaustion.

entries.section: (1) The pursuit of the fleeing Assyrians

paragraphs.text: Making a noise: making a great uproar.
Their heels: the heel is the back of the foot, and what is meant is "behind them."

When the people of Bethulia saw the Assyrians fleeing, they remembered the words of Judith. They hurried after them, shouting with loud voices, asking for the power of God to support them, and blowing the war trumpets to announce their victory.

entries.section: (1) The pursuit of the fleeing Assyrians

paragraphs.text: In one mass: all at once, or as one body.

They poured down upon them in a rush like one powerful projectile aimed at them, which increased the fear and alarm of the Assyrians, so that they scattered in confusion in every direction, which made it easy for the Jews to overtake them and kill them.

Sin makes a person lose his peace, and when he is troubled he falls into greater sins, until he destroys himself by his own agitation. Be strong, take courage, be strengthened, and let your faith be firm, and Satan will not prevail over you.

entries.section: (1) The pursuit of the fleeing Assyrians

paragraphs.text: After them: behind them.
Armed: wearing their weapons.
Their border: their boundaries.

Then Uzziah, the ruler of the city, moved - as a military commander - to play his part behind Judith. He sent messengers to all the cities of Judea to inform them of the news of their victory over the Assyrians and to urge them to pursue them, to kill as many of them as possible, so that the Assyrians, after their flight, would not try to gather their forces and attack the Jews again. So they quickly chose their brave men and went out armed, in large numbers, from all the cities of Israel, to pursue the Assyrians and kill everyone they overtook, and the Assyrians hurried to flee far away from all Judea.

"Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!" (Ps 133:1). For they support one another on the way of spiritual striving. So all the men of the cities of Israel cooperated in pursuing the Assyrians, to receive the blessing of spiritual striving and victory over Satan. In the Church, among your brethren the faithful, you are strengthened in your striving and grow in your love for God, so that you can overthrow all the thoughts of the enemy and he flees from you quickly.

God allowed this so that the people of Bethulia would not be exposed to pride, by feeling that they alone had defeated the Assyrians, but so that the glory would be to God through all His people. Involve others with you as much as you can in prayer, in every spiritual work and in service, so that they receive a blessing from God with you and you are commended. Be like Uzziah, rousing hearts to pursue the way of spiritual striving. And respect the abilities of others with humility, so that you receive the blessing of all.

Show your need of those around you, perhaps by this you will encourage them, especially within the one family, between husband and wife and between brothers, and not only from children to parents, but from parents to children. Thus you encourage the faint-hearted and gladden hearts, and then you praise everyone with love and appreciation.

entries.section: (1) The pursuit of the fleeing Assyrians

paragraphs.text: They were enriched: they became wealthy.

When the Assyrians fled and moved far from Bethulia, the rest of its inhabitants went out to gather the great spoils which the Assyrians had left in their tents: gold, silver, clothing, furniture and many belongings. For the Assyrians carried with them all the needs they required for travel over long months, so these tents were like permanent houses, because the Assyrians had conquered many peoples and taken from them countless spoils, and their tents were full of spoils. They also left behind large flocks of sheep and cattle and all the beasts. As for the men of war from Bethulia, when they returned to their city they carried spoils from the camp of the Assyrians, as much as they were able to carry, so all the inhabitants of Bethulia became rich.

Thus the little city of Bethulia became very great, and became the richest of the cities of Israel, and from it came the savior of all the people of God, that is, Judith. She is a symbol of Bethlehem, from which came Christ, the Savior of the whole world, of which the prophets testified, saying: "And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel" (Mt 2:6). God is wonderful, who makes the rich poor and the poor rich. Everything the Assyrians had gathered of wealth and glory they lost in one day, and even lost their lives, because they relied on their own strength. But those who trusted in God endured affliction to the end, and began to fall from thirst and were near death and in great poverty, and their great God turned their mourning into joy and their poverty into limitless riches. Blessed is the one who trusts in You, O Lord; truly in the day of evil You deliver him and lift him above his enemies, and enrich him from Your riches, and he rejoices and praises You.

Support me, O Lord, that I may not faint under the pressure of affliction, but trust in You and persevere in my prayers, confident that You do not forget me, and that You will surely give me victory over my enemies, rescue me from every sin and enrich my life with every virtue, so that my heart may meditate on Your praise.

entries.section: (2) Joakim blesses Judith

paragraphs.text: When the news of the victory over the Assyrians spread throughout Israel and Jerusalem, the great priest Joiakim, or Eliakim, came from Jerusalem, with the priests and elders of the Jews who lived in Jerusalem, to Bethulia, to meet the great saint Judith, by whose hand God saved His people.

entries.section: (2) Joakim blesses Judith

paragraphs.text: When they arrived at Bethulia and entered the house of Judith and saw her, they rejoiced greatly and blessed her, glorifying God, declaring to her that she had become the cause of the glory, joy and pride of all the Jews by this deed of hers, that is, the killing of Holofernes.

entries.section: (2) Joakim blesses Judith

paragraphs.text: Might: strength.

They praised her courage and strength, as well as the steadfastness of her faith in facing the mighty Holofernes and killing him, in addition to her love of purity and chastity, for after her widowhood she devoted herself to worship; therefore God supported her and completed the victory for her. She is great and blessed, not only in this life, but also for ever in heaven.

entries.section: (2) Joakim blesses Judith

paragraphs.text: After Joiakim and his elders had said these words, all the people present at this reception confirmed all that they had said, with confidence, strength and joy.

In this way the Fathers, the bishops and the patriarchs, sought the blessing of the saints in the deserts. And even now the Church glorifies her children the martyrs and saints throughout the ages. Your taking part in the celebrations and glorification of the saints rouses your heart to pursue the way of God and kindles your love toward Him. You are a member of the Church; everything good that you do is ascribed to her, and likewise every evil that you commit stains her brow. So try to gladden the heart of your mother the Church, that she may be proud of you.

entries.section: (2) Plundering the spoils of the Assyrians

paragraphs.text: The people of Bethulia - joined by some soldiers of the Jews from the other cities, returning from the pursuit of the Assyrians - continued carrying the spoils from the tents of the Assyrians, which numbered tens of thousands. Each tent had a separate dwelling, full of precious things, not only of what they had taken from Assyria, but even more of what they had plundered from the nations they had occupied.

The people of Bethulia carried the spoils to their houses, then returned to carry a second and a third time, and they continued like this for more than a month, gathering each day from the abundant spoils of the camp of the Assyrians.

The blessings of God to His children are very many, as the Scripture says: "The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it" (Prov 10:22). God is rich; He has much without limit and wants to give to you. What matters is that you hold fast to your sonship to Him and seek His Person, that is, the Kingdom of God, that it may reign over your heart; then He gives you the rest of your needs, that is, all material things, in great abundance.

entries.section: (2) Plundering the spoils of the Assyrians

paragraphs.text: As for Judith, all the people were searching for any means to honor her. While they were plundering the spoils, they gathered everything in the tent of Holofernes and the other tents pitched beside it, in which his belongings were, such as vessels of gold and silver, that is, all his treasures, and presented them to Judith as a gift of love, in gratitude for her kindness and in honor of her deed.

The saints who fled from material things and honor and became strangers to the world have been greatly honored by God throughout history, and He has bestowed gifts upon them abundantly, not only on earth but even more in heaven. And when we are raised to heaven on the last day, the places that were emptied by the fall of the demons will be filled by the holy children of God, just as Judith was given the tent of Holofernes, that is, his dwelling.

entries.section: (2) Plundering the spoils of the Assyrians

paragraphs.text: Harps: plural of harp, a stringed musical instrument.

When all hearts in Bethulia were filled with joy, the young men and women hurried to the house of Judith, and the women surrounded her, and each one carried whatever musical instruments were common at that time, namely lutes and harps, to sing and chant to God and to honor their great heroine Judith.

Do not forget to thank God for the works of His care for you every day in your prayers and your praises. And do not neglect also to honor everyone who deserves honor, with kind words and by every means, so that you rejoice and gladden hearts: "honour to whom honour" (Rom 13:7). Thanking God and the greatness of Judith

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: Timbrels: plural of timbrel, which are copper discs counted among the percussion instruments and used in churches.
Cymbals: either copper discs that are struck, producing a loud sound, or stringed instruments.

The celebration began, with Judith leading the procession of praise to God, and around her the women and the young men, repeating after her the song of victory, using every musical instrument they had, to proclaim with all their strength their joy in the Lord and to glorify Him.
This hymn is regarded as a psalm, or a song of Judith, similar to the psalms of David the prophet, and in it God is magnified, who triumphed over the enemies.

The use of music is ancient, used by man from the beginning of his life, as the Book of Genesis tells us (Gen 4:21, 22). David the prophet is counted among the most famous of those who used music to accompany the recitation of the psalms. Also known in this field is Miriam, the sister of Moses.
Judith is a symbol of Christ, or of the priest who leads the people in praising God, who alone has authority over our lives.

Judith rouses the people with the timbrels and cymbals, with their loud sounds, to join her in praising God, and in this she is a symbol of the servant who awakens everyone who is lax, to glorify God and offer Him a new song, different from the earlier songs and prayers of his life, which he offered lukewarmly.

Our praise of God in the New Testament is a new praise, for God showed on the Cross a love that surpasses understanding, which was not revealed to men throughout the Old Testament, and He did a work in men that He had not done before, for He renewed their nature by the second birth in Baptism. And He gave them His most holy Body and Blood in the sacrament of the Eucharist. Would that we would rise spiritually with zeal and care, to sing the song of love to God, who is glorified in a new way in our lives every day.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: Brings to nothing: crushes and destroys.

The Lord is great above all the gods of the nations and all the powers of the world, and if He enters a war, He is certainly the victor and crushes His enemies. His name is the Lord, that is, the Master of all creatures. He was pleased to dwell in the midst of His people, to declare that He is their God, their defender and their deliverer from every evil. Because of the greatness of God's power in defending His people, the ancient pagans thought that the God of Israel was a god of war, and so they feared His people.
Let us enjoy being in the Church, because Emmanuel our God dwells in our midst and blesses all His children, and even unites with them in Holy Communion.

Do you give God a place in your heart, that He may dwell in you, keep you and remove every sin from you? Open your heart in humility to prayers, spiritual readings and meditation, and you will enjoy His indwelling in you by His Holy Spirit and His working in complete freedom.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: The valleys: the low places.

As the armies of the Assyrians crushed many nations on their way from the north-east, they increased in strength through the multitude of their followers and their weapons. They had set out from Assyria one hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers, in addition to twelve thousand horsemen, and tens of thousands of young captives joined them, whom they had added to themselves from the occupied lands. So the movement of these thousands was frightening, blocking all the roads and valleys, and the whole strength of the cities collapsed before them.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: Trusting in their strength, the Assyrians were determined to burn the city of Bethulia, because it had closed its gates in their face, as they had burned many of the cities they attacked, and they threatened to kill and wipe out great and small, young men and children, men and women.

Do not be alarmed by the visible strength of men and their threats, knowing that the power of God is above every power. Stand firm in your faith and close the doors of your senses to sin, and trust that the Lord who dwells in you keeps you pure and no one will harm you, but you will increase in joy and praise every day.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: Smites: destroys.

Titan: a Greek god distinguished by strength in war. The Valley of the Rephaim was called the valley of the sons of Titan, and it is a fertile valley, lying south-west of Jerusalem (2 Sam 5:18). The Rephaim are distinguished by their strength and the height of their stature, and perhaps this is the reason for naming their valley the valley of the sons of Titan.

The war is not against the people of God, but against God Himself, who dwells in their midst. Therefore it is the Lord who crushed Holofernes and delivered him into the hand of Judith to kill him. God has no need of the strength of young men, or of the giants and mighty men of the world, to accomplish His purposes; the hands of a woman of weak frame, whom God had endowed with beauty, are enough for Him, and He is glorified in her weakness, for the strength is from God, and He can use any instrument, however weak it may seem.

Do not look at your weakness and helplessness before the difficulty of the problem or the power of sin, for God is the One who fights for you, and He is able to crush any power under your feet, so that it appears that you are the victor, although it is He who is victorious in you.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: She put on: she put on, that is, she wore.

When the hour of striving and war came, Judith took off the clothes of widowhood, which point to weakness, since she had no husband to protect and defend her, and put on instead her garments of joy, not to satisfy her desire and be vain of her beauty, but to gladden the hearts of her people. She put on these clothes for her heavenly Bridegroom, who gladdens her heart and saves her and all her people and delights their hearts. Thus the weak woman became strong, because she had obtained God as her Bridegroom, and He is stronger than any husband in the world.

If you feel that you have no support and no strength in the world to rely on, like a widow, then you can lift your eyes to Christ, the Bridegroom of your soul, and you will be strengthened and rejoice all your days.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: She completed her adornment by putting ointments on her face, to be beautiful before God, so that Holofernes would fall under her feet.

The ointment of your face is the sweat of spiritual striving mingled with the tears of repentance flowing down your cheeks, so that your face is perfumed before God, who "offered Himself an acceptable sacrifice on the Cross, and His good Father smelled it in the evening on Golgotha" (a hymn sung on Great Friday). As for her hair, flowing in beautiful tresses, which is the pride and crown of every woman, Judith gathered it and bound it with a shining crown which she wore on her head, and she appeared more beautiful. This crown is her faith in God, to whom she submits and who adorns her head, and He gives her complete salvation. She put on her spiritual weapon, her faith in God the Savior, that is, "the helmet of salvation" (Eph 6:17). And she armed herself with the rest of her weapons against Holofernes, for she put on her splendid garments, that is, all her weapons, to overthrow him.
Do not neglect any of the means of grace, to defeat the wars of the devil.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: In the end she put on beautiful shining sandals on her feet, which drew his eyes and captured his heart, so that he was humbled by lust under her feet. Then it was easy for her to kill him with his own weapon, since he had become very humbled and weak.

Be sure that you have authority over the whole world, and you can tread on serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy. So do not give up your authority, lest lust humble you and you strike yourself down, that is, you die by your own dagger and perish by your own lust.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: All the power of Persia and Media, subject to the empire of Assyria and represented in the chief of its armies Holofernes and all his armies, was alarmed and terrified before the courage of Judith and all the people of God.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: The weak men appeared, faint from extreme thirst but trusting in God, and all the Assyrians cried out and fled before them, because God was glorified in their weakness, and the flame of thirst in the throat of the people of God burned the wicked and killed them. Truly, as God said, "for my strength is made perfect in weakness" (2 Cor 12:9).

The labors of your fasting, your hunger and your thirst, your humbling yourself in prostrations (metanoias) and your tears poured out before God burn up every sin and defeat the tyranny of the devil. It was by thirst and hunger that the saints roamed the deserts, trampling all the power of the devil.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: They wounded them: they multiplied the wounds in them.

In the eyes of the Assyrians the Jews were slaves to them, like the rest of the nations. So the people of Bethulia, who were - in the eyes of the Assyrians - the sons of slave girls, went out and attacked their camp, and killed them easily. The giants of the Assyrians were like boys in the hands of the Jews, who overcame them, and the Assyrians fled in fear. All this killing and wounding was by the power of God, at the hands of the weak and humble, the people of God who trust in Him.
Do not be troubled if people despise you; you will surely prevail in the end, and God will be glorified in you, and the devil who also despises you will be crushed by God under your feet.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: Judith called all who heard her a second time to praise God and to sing with new zeal and strength.

entries.section: (1) The hymn of Judith

paragraphs.text: Adonai: the name of God in the Old Testament, representing the awesome God before whom every soul bows in reverence, and the special God of His people, who defends and protects them.
